scenarios.title: Bargaining for Tomatoes at the Market
scenarios.description: You are at Mokolo Market in Douala. You want to buy tomatoes for your family. Practice asking prices and making offers.

start.text: Hello! Fresh tomatoes here! Very sweet and red. How many piles do you want today?

options.text: How much are they?
options.feedback: Good start. Before saying how many piles you want, you ask about the price using a clear question.

options.text: I want one pile, but how much is it?
options.feedback: Very good. You say the quantity and also ask the price in one polite sentence.

options.text: Yes.
options.feedback: This does not answer the seller’s question. Say how many piles you want or ask about the price.

step2.text: For you, only 500 CFA for one pile.

options.text: That is too expensive! I will give you 300 CFA for one pile.
options.feedback: Good bargaining language. You react to the price and make a clear counter-offer using “I will give you…”.

options.text: Okay, here is 500 CFA for one pile.
options.feedback: This is correct and polite, but you do not bargain. In markets like Mokolo, sellers often expect some negotiation.

options.text: No, I do not want them.
options.feedback: You refuse too quickly. Try bargaining first; the seller may reduce the price if you negotiate politely.

step3.text: Ah, my friend, 300 is too small! These tomatoes are very fresh. Give me 400, and I will add extra tomatoes for you.

options.text: They look good. I will give you 350 CFA for one pile.
options.feedback: Nice counter-offer. You show you accept the good quality but still try to get a better price.

options.text: Okay, 400 is fine. Thank you.
options.feedback: You accept the seller’s counter-offer and keep good relations. You bargain only once but still get extra tomatoes.

options.text: No, 250 CFA.
options.feedback: You go much lower than the seller’s price. This keeps the bargaining going, but it may sound aggressive in a friendly market conversation.

step4.text: My friend, 250 is too low. You will finish my business! I cannot sell at that price. Let us be serious. How much can you really pay?

options.text: Okay, I can really pay 320 CFA for one pile.
options.feedback: You move closer to the seller’s price. This is a more realistic offer and helps you reach an agreement.

options.text: If you do not take 250, I will go to another seller.
options.feedback: You are threatening to leave very early. This can damage the relationship. Try adjusting your offer instead of giving an ultimatum.

options.text: I do not have money.
options.feedback: You already started bargaining. It is better to give a serious price you can pay, not say you have no money now.

step5.text: Hmm… 320 is still a bit low. Let us meet in the middle. Give me 350 CFA, and I promise to add some extra tomatoes for you.

options.text: Okay, 350 CFA. That is good. Please add the extra tomatoes.
options.feedback: You accept a fair middle price and speak politely. This is a realistic and successful bargain.

options.text: Cut the price to 330 CFA, and I will buy one pile.
options.feedback: You keep negotiating but move closer to the seller’s price. This is strong bargaining; be ready to accept the next offer.

options.text: No, I will go to another seller.
options.feedback: You walk away after reaching almost a fair agreement. Sometimes accepting a reasonable price is better than starting again elsewhere.

step6_no_bargain.text: You are a tough customer! Listen, 330 CFA is my last price. Take it or leave it.

options.text: Alright, I will take one pile for 330 CFA. Thank you very much.
options.feedback: You accept the final offer and stay polite. You used bargaining to get a better price than 500 CFA.

options.text: Give me two piles for 600 CFA.
options.feedback: Now you ask for an even bigger discount after the seller’s final price. This is unrealistic and can make the seller unhappy.

options.text: No, still too expensive. I am leaving.
options.feedback: You refuse after the seller has already come down a lot. In real markets, this is likely a good price; you are missing a useful deal.

step6_final.text: You are a tough customer! Listen, 330 CFA is my last price. Take it or leave it.

options.text: Alright, I will take one pile for 330 CFA. Thank you very much.
options.feedback: You accept the final offer and stay polite. You used bargaining to get a better price than 500 CFA.

options.text: Give me two piles for 600 CFA.
options.feedback: Now you ask for an even bigger discount after the seller’s final price. This is unrealistic and can make the seller unhappy.

options.text: No, still too expensive. I am leaving.
options.feedback: You refuse after the seller has already come down a lot. In real markets, this is likely a good price; you are missing a useful deal.

step7.text: Thank you, my friend. Here are your tomatoes. Enjoy your meal with your family!

options.text: Here is the money. Thank you, have a nice day.
options.feedback: Excellent closing. You pay, say thank you, and add a friendly goodbye. This is polite and natural in the market.

options.text: Give me the tomatoes first. I will pay later.
options.feedback: At markets, you normally pay immediately. Asking to pay later can make the seller distrust you.

options.text: Thanks.
options.feedback: This is short but acceptable. To sound more polite and confident, you can say, “Thank you, have a good day.”

scenarios.title: Buying Cloth at the Material Shop
scenarios.description: You are at the material shop in Buea Town. You need to buy cloth to make a new dress or shirt.

start.text: Good morning! Welcome to my shop. What are you looking for today?

options.text: Good morning. I need cloth for a dress.
options.feedback: Very clear. You greet the shopkeeper and say exactly what you need.

options.text: I am looking.
options.feedback: This answer is too vague. Say what you need, for example: “I need cloth for a dress” or “I want cloth for a shirt.”

options.text: How much?
options.feedback: The shopkeeper does not know what you want yet. First say what you are looking for, then ask about the price.

step2.text: Okay, cloth for a dress. Is it for everyday use or for a special occasion? And do you prefer cotton or something shiny like satin?

options.text: It is for everyday use. I want cotton cloth.
options.feedback: Good answer. You explain the use and the type of fabric you want.

options.text: It is for a wedding. I want something shiny.
options.feedback: Clear description. You say it is for a special occasion and choose a shiny material.

options.text: Just cloth, any kind.
options.feedback: This does not help the shopkeeper. Say if it is for everyday or special use and what type you prefer.

step3.text: Good. I have many colors. I have blue, red, green, yellow, and white. Which color do you like?

options.text: I like blue. Show me the blue cloth, please.
options.feedback: Good polite sentence. You say what you like and add “please.”

options.text: Blue.
options.feedback: The color is correct, but the sentence is too short. Be polite and complete: “I like blue. Show me the blue cloth, please.”

options.text: All of them.
options.feedback: You cannot choose all the colors. Pick one color you really want, for example “blue” or “green.”

step4.text: This blue cloth is very nice. It is soft and strong. How many yards do you want?

options.text: I want 3 yards. Is it good quality?
options.feedback: Very good. You say the number of yards and ask about quality in one clear sentence.

options.text: How much does it cost for one yard?
options.feedback: This is also a useful question, but the shopkeeper asked about quantity. After you hear the price, you still need to say how many yards you want.

options.text: Give me some cloth.
options.feedback: “Some cloth” is not specific. Say a number like “3 yards” or “4 yards.”

step5.text: Yes, the quality is very good. For this cloth, it is 2000 CFA for one yard. If you take 3 yards, the price is 6000 CFA.

options.text: That is too much. Can you give me a lower price?
options.feedback: Good use of bargaining language: you react to the price and politely ask for a lower price.

options.text: Okay, I will take 3 yards for 6000 CFA.
options.feedback: You accept the price and make a clear decision, but you do not negotiate. In many cloth shops, bargaining is possible.

options.text: I do not have enough money. Can I take only 2 yards?
options.feedback: This is a good way to adjust your order. You change the quantity to match your budget.

step6.text: My friend, this is good cloth. The price is fair. But because you are a good customer, I can reduce a little. For 3 yards, I can give you 5800 CFA. If you want only 2 yards, it will be 3800 CFA.

options.text: Thank you very much! I will take 3 yards for 5800 CFA.
options.feedback: You accept the discount politely and still get the amount of cloth you wanted.

options.text: No, give me 3 yards for 5000 CFA.
options.feedback: You are asking for a much lower price after the shopkeeper already reduced it. This may sound too aggressive in a friendly negotiation.

options.text: Okay, I will take 2 yards for 3800 CFA, please.
options.feedback: You choose the smaller quantity to spend less money. This is a practical and polite decision.

step7.text: Thank you. Here is your cloth. I hope your dress will be very beautiful.

options.text: Here is the money. Thank you for your help.
options.feedback: Good closing. You pay, thank the shopkeeper, and show appreciation.

options.text: Can I pay next week?
options.feedback: In most cloth shops, you pay immediately. Asking to pay next week is not usual unless you know the shopkeeper very well.

options.text: Thanks. I will come back again.
options.feedback: Friendly and natural ending. You thank the shopkeeper and show that you may return.

scenarios.title: Asking for Fish at the Fish Stall
scenarios.description: You are at the fish stall in the market. You want to buy fresh fish for your family's meal.

start.text: Hello! I have fresh fish today. Big ones and small ones. What do you want?

options.text: I want fresh fish for cooking. How much is one piece?
options.feedback: Very clear. You say what you want and ask about the price of one piece.

options.text: I want fish.
options.feedback: This is correct but not complete. Also ask about the price or size, for example: “I want fish. How much is one piece?”

options.text: Give me the best fish.
options.feedback: “Best” is not clear. Ask about the type or size and say how many pieces you want.

step2.text: I have big tilapia for 3000 CFA per piece, and small fish for 1500 CFA per piece. The big ones are better for cooking with soup.

options.text: Give me three big tilapia, please.
options.feedback: Good choice. You say the number, the type, and use “please.”

options.text: Which fish is better for soup, big or small?
options.feedback: Good question. You ask for advice based on your cooking plan.

options.text: I want the cheap ones.
options.feedback: You only talk about price. Also think about cooking. Ask which fish is better for your meal, not only which is cheaper.

step3.text: The big tilapia are best for soup. They are very fresh. How many big ones do you want?

options.text: Give me three big tilapia, please. Are they really fresh?
options.feedback: Excellent. You give a clear number and ask a question about freshness.

options.text: Just give me some fish.
options.feedback: “Some fish” is not specific. Say exactly how many pieces you want.

options.text: Two big tilapia is enough.
options.feedback: Clear and specific. You adjust the quantity according to your needs.

step4.text: Good choice! I caught them this morning. Do you want me to clean them for you?

options.text: Yes, please clean them for me. Thank you.
options.feedback: Polite and clear. You accept the cleaning service and say “thank you.”

options.text: No, I will clean them at home.
options.feedback: This is also fine. You clearly say you prefer to clean them yourself.

options.text: How much more if you clean them?
options.feedback: In many markets in Cameroon, cleaning the fish is included in the price. The seller did not say there is extra cost, so you do not need to ask this.

step5.text: Okay. So, big tilapia at 3000 CFA each. The total is 9000 CFA (or 6000 CFA).

options.text: That is too much. Can you make it 8000 CFA?
options.feedback: Good bargaining language. You react to the total price and make a counter-offer.

options.text: Okay, here is the full amount.
options.feedback: You pay the exact total and finish the purchase, but you do not try to negotiate.

options.text: I only have 7000 CFA. Give me fewer pieces instead.
options.feedback: Clever solution. You adjust the quantity to match your money.

step6.text: My friend, the fish is very fresh and I am cleaning it. 9000 is a fair price. But I can reduce a little. I will take 8500 CFA. If you want fewer pieces, you can also take two for 6000.

options.text: Thank you. I will take all the fish for 8500 CFA.
options.feedback: You accept the discount politely and keep the full quantity.

options.text: No, 8000 CFA or nothing.
options.feedback: You push again after the seller already reduced the price. This can sound too hard in a friendly market negotiation.

options.text: Okay, I will just take two fish for 6000 CFA, please.
options.feedback: You choose the smaller option. This is a reasonable and polite decision if your money is limited.

step7.text: Here are your fish. Thank you for buying. Enjoy your meal with your family!

options.text: Here is the money. Thank you very much. Have a nice day.
options.feedback: Very polite and natural closing. You pay and say thank you and goodbye.

options.text: Give me the fish first. I will bring the money later.
options.feedback: At the market, you should pay immediately. Asking to pay later can make the seller distrust you.

options.text: Thanks.
options.feedback: Short but acceptable. For better practice, you can say a full sentence like “Thank you, see you next time.”

scenarios.title: Buying Medicine at the Pharmacy
scenarios.description: You have a headache and a small fever. You go to the pharmacy to buy medicine.

start.text: Good afternoon! What can I help you with today?

options.text: Good afternoon. I have a headache and a small fever. Can you help me?
options.feedback: Very clear and polite. You greet and describe your problem.

options.text: I am not well.
options.feedback: This is too general. Say what is wrong, for example: “I have a headache and a fever.”

options.text: Do you have medicine?
options.feedback: The pharmacist needs to know your problem first. Then they can choose the right medicine.

step2.text: I see. When did this start? Since yesterday or today?

options.text: It started this morning. I woke up with a headache.
options.feedback: Good answer. You say clearly when it started.

options.text: It started yesterday evening.
options.feedback: Also good. You give useful information about the time.

options.text: I do not know.
options.feedback: Try to remember. The pharmacist needs to know when your symptoms started to help you.

step3.text: Alright. Do you have any other symptoms? For example, nausea, sore throat, or body pain?

options.text: I feel a little weak, but no nausea and no sore throat.
options.feedback: Clear and detailed. You say what you have and what you do not have.

options.text: It is just the headache and the fever.
options.feedback: Good. You confirm that there are no other symptoms.

options.text: It is bad.
options.feedback: “Bad” is not specific. Explain exactly what you feel (weakness, nausea, sore throat, etc.).

step4.text: Okay. It seems like a simple headache and mild fever. I can give you aspirin to help. Take two tablets with water, three times a day.

options.text: Thank you. Is it safe? Are there any side effects?
options.feedback: Excellent. You ask about safety and side effects before accepting the medicine.

options.text: Okay, give me the medicine.
options.feedback: You should ask about safety, side effects, and price before you accept.

options.text: How much does it cost?
options.feedback: Asking the price is important. You will still need information about side effects.

step5.text: Aspirin is generally safe. Some people have a small stomach pain, but that is rare. Most people have no problem if they take it with food.

options.text: Okay, I understand. How much is one box?
options.feedback: Good. You show that you understood the information and now ask about the price.

options.text: I do not want it if there are side effects.
options.feedback: Side effects are rare and usually small. The pharmacist says it is safe for most people. It is better to listen and then decide calmly.

options.text: How exactly should I take it? With food or without?
options.feedback: Very good question. You ask clearly about how to use the medicine.

step6.text: Take two tablets three times a day with food and plenty of water. One box of aspirin is 1200 CFA. If the fever does not go away after two days, you should see a doctor.

options.text: Thank you. I will take it as you said. Here is 1200 CFA.
options.feedback: You repeat the instructions in your mind, accept the advice, and pay. Very good.

options.text: Can I get a lower price?
options.feedback: Pharmacy prices are usually fixed. You cannot bargain here like in the market.

options.text: Do I need to see a doctor now, or only if it does not get better?
options.feedback: Good follow-up question. You show that you want to be careful about your health.

step7.text: You can try this medicine first. If you still have fever after two days, then see a doctor. Take care of yourself and rest.

options.text: Okay, thank you very much for your help. I will rest and come back if it does not improve.
options.feedback: Polite and complete. You show you understood the instructions.

options.text: I will take more tablets if the pain is strong.
options.feedback: Do not take more than the pharmacist’s instructions. More medicine is not always better and can be dangerous.

options.text: Thanks. I understand what to do now.
options.feedback: Clear and friendly ending. You confirm you understand and say thank you.

scenarios.title: Negotiating Taxi Fare
scenarios.description: You are at the taxi stand and you want to go to town. You need to ask where he is going and how much it will cost.

start.text: Hello! Where do you want to go?

options.text: I want to go to town. How much do you charge?
options.feedback: Very clear. You say your destination and ask about the price.

options.text: Town.
options.feedback: This is too short. Use a full sentence and ask about price, for example: “I want to go to town. How much do you charge?”

options.text: Is this taxi going to town?
options.feedback: Good question. You check the destination first. You still need to ask about the price.

step2.text: Okay, town. For you, the price is 2500 CFA.

options.text: That is too expensive. Can you make it 2000 CFA?
options.feedback: Good bargaining language. You react to the price and make a polite counter-offer.

options.text: Okay, I will pay 2500 CFA.
options.feedback: You accept the price and can start the trip, but you miss the chance to negotiate.

options.text: How much do the other taxis charge?
options.feedback: Do not talk about other taxis with this driver. Negotiate directly with the person in front of you.

step3.text: My friend, 2500 is the normal price. Fuel is expensive. But I can take you for 2300 CFA because you are a nice person.

options.text: Thank you. 2300 is good. Let us go.
options.feedback: You accept the discount politely and can start the trip.

options.text: That is still too much. I only have 2000 CFA.
options.feedback: You explain your real limit. This keeps the negotiation open in an honest way.

options.text: No, 2000 CFA or I will find another taxi.
options.feedback: You are giving a hard ultimatum after the driver already reduced the price. This can sound rude.

step4.text: You only have 2000? Hmm… This is a problem. But I will help you today. Give me 2000 now, and you owe me 300. You can give it to me tomorrow.

options.text: Thank you! That is very kind. I promise I will pay you the 300 CFA tomorrow.
options.feedback: You accept the driver’s help, show gratitude, and clearly promise to pay later.

options.text: No, I cannot owe you money. I will find another taxi.
options.feedback: The driver is offering a generous solution. Refusing quickly means you lose a chance for help.

options.text: Can you take 2000 CFA and I do not owe you anything?
options.feedback: You are asking for more after the driver already tried to help. This may sound unfair.

step5.text: Alright, get in. We will go to town now.

options.text: Thank you. How long will it take to reach town?
options.feedback: Good question. You check the approximate travel time.

options.text: Just drive.
options.feedback: This sounds a bit rude. It is better to thank the driver and maybe ask about time or traffic.

options.text: Can we avoid the traffic if possible?
options.feedback: Polite request. You think about traffic and comfort.

step6.text: We are here. This is town. Please pay the agreed amount.

options.text: Here is the money. Thank you for the ride.
options.feedback: Polite and complete. You pay and say thank you.

options.text: Can you reduce the price now that we are here?
options.feedback: You already agreed on a price before the trip. It is not polite to ask for a discount after you arrive.

options.text: I forgot my money. I will pay another day.
options.feedback: This creates a big problem. Always check that you have enough money before entering the taxi.

scenarios.title: Buying Phone Credit at a Kiosk
scenarios.description: Your phone is running out of credit. You go to the mobile money kiosk near your house.

start.text: Good morning! What do you need?

options.text: Good morning. I need phone credit for MTN, please.
options.feedback: Very clear and polite. You say you need credit and for which company.

options.text: Phone credit.
options.feedback: This is not complete. Say which company you use, for example: “I need phone credit for MTN.”

options.text: Give me credit.
options.feedback: Too direct. Be polite and say “please”, and also say the company: “Please give me phone credit for MTN.”

step2.text: Okay, MTN. Do you want a scratch card, or should I put the credit directly on your phone?

options.text: Please put the credit directly on my phone. This is my number: [say number].
options.feedback: Very good. You choose direct top-up and give your number clearly.

options.text: I want a scratch card, please.
options.feedback: Also good. You clearly say you want a scratch card.

options.text: Any way is fine.
options.feedback: The operator needs to know exactly which method you prefer. Choose “direct top-up” or “scratch card.”

step3.text: Alright. How much do you want? I have 500 CFA, 1000 CFA, 2000 CFA, 5000 CFA, and 10000 CFA.

options.text: I want 2000 CFA credit, please.
options.feedback: Clear and polite. You choose a specific amount.

options.text: Give me the big one.
options.feedback: “The big one” is not clear. Say the exact amount, for example: “I want 5000 CFA credit.”

options.text: How much is the biggest one?
options.feedback: He already told you the biggest amount is 10000 CFA. Just choose one of the options.

step4.text: Good. I will send 2000 CFA to your number now. You will receive a message. Okay?

options.text: Yes, I understand. Thank you.
options.feedback: You show that you understand the process.

options.text: Please, how do I use the code on my phone?
options.feedback: Good question. You ask for extra instructions if you are not sure.

options.text: Just give me the credit now. I do not need an explanation.
options.feedback: It is important to listen and understand how it works, especially if you are not experienced with credit.

step5.text: So that is 2000 CFA. Can you give me the money now?

options.text: Yes, here is 2000 CFA.
options.feedback: Correct. You pay the exact amount.

options.text: I only have 1500 CFA. Can I give you that?
options.feedback: This credit costs 2000 CFA. If you do not have enough, you must choose a smaller amount, like 1000 CFA.

options.text: Can you make it 1500 CFA?
options.feedback: Phone credit prices are fixed. You cannot bargain like in the market.

step6.text: Thank you. Your credit is ready. You can check your balance on your phone.

options.text: Thank you very much. I will check my balance now.
options.feedback: Polite and complete ending.

options.text: If it does not work, I will come back.
options.feedback: Reasonable. You show you know what to do if there is a problem.

options.text: Next time, give me a better price.
options.feedback: Prices are fixed for phone credit. Asking for a better price sounds strange here.

scenarios.title: Renting a House (Asking About Price and Terms)
scenarios.description: You are looking for a house to rent in your neighborhood. You see a house for rent with a sign.

start.text: Good afternoon! Can I help you?

options.text: Good afternoon. Is this house for rent?
options.feedback: Very clear and polite. You ask directly about the house.

options.text: I want to rent.
options.feedback: Say what you want to rent, for example: “I want to rent this house.”

options.text: How much?
options.feedback: First ask if the house is for rent. Then you can ask about the price.

step2.text: Yes, the house is for rent. It has three bedrooms, a kitchen, a living room, and a small yard. It is very nice and clean.

options.text: How much is the rent per month?
options.feedback: Good. You ask about the monthly rent clearly.

options.text: It looks good.
options.feedback: It is fine to say that, but you should also ask about the price and conditions.

options.text: Can I see inside now?
options.feedback: First check if you can afford it by asking about the rent.

step3.text: The rent is 60000 CFA per month. You need to pay two months in advance and one month as a guarantee.

options.text: So I need to pay 180000 CFA to move in?
options.feedback: Good calculation. You show you understand 3 months × 60000 = 180000 CFA.

options.text: That is too much! Can you make it 40000?
options.feedback: House rent is usually fixed. It is better to ask more questions or look for another house, not bargain like at the market.

options.text: When can I move in?
options.feedback: First show that you understand the payment terms (three months in total), then ask about moving in.

step4.text: Yes, exactly. 60000 times three is 180000 CFA. You pay this, and the house is yours. You can move in the next day.

options.text: Okay, but is there water and electricity?
options.feedback: Very important question. You ask about utilities before deciding.

options.text: Perfect! I will pay tomorrow.
options.feedback: Before you decide to pay, you should ask about water, electricity, and maybe other conditions.

options.text: Do I need to sign a paper or contract?
options.feedback: Also a very good question. Renting a house usually comes with a contract.

step5.text: Yes, we have water from the tap and electricity. We also have a small generator when the power goes off. I have a contract for you to sign. It explains the rules for using the house.

options.text: Thank you. Can I see the house inside before I decide?
options.feedback: Excellent. You ask to see inside before paying.

options.text: What are the rules in the contract?
options.feedback: Good. You show that you want to understand the rules clearly.

options.text: Okay, I will take it. Here is the money.
options.feedback: You should see the inside and read or hear the rules before giving money.

step6.text: No problem. I will show you inside and tell you the main rules. If you like it, we can sign the contract.

options.text: Thank you. If everything is okay inside, I will come back tomorrow with the 180000 CFA.
options.feedback: Careful and polite. You give yourself time to decide and prepare the money.

options.text: I like it. Can we sign the contract and I move in next week?
options.feedback: Clear decision and good use of future plans (“move in next week”).

options.text: I am not sure. I will think about it and call you later.
options.feedback: Also acceptable. You do not have to decide immediately.

scenarios.title: Buying School Supplies
scenarios.description: School is starting next week and you need to buy notebooks, pens, and a schoolbag.

start.text: Hello! Welcome! School is starting soon, yes?

options.text: Yes, I need to buy school supplies. Do you have notebooks?
options.feedback: Clear and specific. You say what you need and ask about notebooks.

options.text: I need things for school.
options.feedback: This is too general. Say which things: notebooks, pens, a schoolbag, etc.

options.text: How much is everything?
options.feedback: First say what you want to buy, then ask about prices.

step2.text: Of course! I have good notebooks. Large ones and small ones. Which do you prefer?

options.text: I want large notebooks. How much do they cost?
options.feedback: Good. You choose a type and ask for the price.

options.text: Give me notebooks.
options.feedback: Say “please” and also say which type and how many, for example: “Please give me three large notebooks.”

options.text: What is the difference between large and small?
options.feedback: Good question. After the explanation, you should choose one type.

step3.text: One large notebook is 800 CFA. Small ones are 500 CFA. How many large notebooks do you want?

options.text: I need three large notebooks, please.
options.feedback: Clear and polite. You say the exact number.

options.text: Give me a lot of notebooks.
options.feedback: “A lot” is not clear. Say a number: two, three, five, etc.

options.text: Can I buy two large and one small notebook?
options.feedback: Good mixed choice. You still use numbers clearly.

step4.text: Good! So the notebooks are [calculate total]. Now, do you need pens and a schoolbag?

options.text: Yes, I need pens and a schoolbag too.
options.feedback: Clear. You say exactly what else you want.

options.text: Yes, everything.
options.feedback: “Everything” is not specific. Say what you mean: pens, a schoolbag, ruler, etc.

options.text: Just notebooks for now, thank you.
options.feedback: This is fine if you only want notebooks today.

step5.text: Okay! I have blue pens, red pens, and black pens. One pen is 150 CFA. And I have schoolbags from 3000 CFA to 8000 CFA.

options.text: I want four pens – two blue and two red. And show me the schoolbags around 4000 CFA, please.
options.feedback: Very clear. You specify number, colors, and bag price range.

options.text: Give me pens and a bag.
options.feedback: Be specific: how many pens, which colors, and what price range for the bag.

options.text: What is the best schoolbag?
options.feedback: “Best” depends on you and your budget. First say how much you want to spend.

step6.text: Good choice! Here is a strong schoolbag for 4500 CFA. It has many pockets. The colors are red, blue, and black.

options.text: I like the blue one. What is the total price for everything?
options.feedback: You choose a color and ask for the total. Very good.

options.text: It is too expensive. Show me a cheaper bag around 3000 CFA, please.
options.feedback: Polite and clear. You ask to see a cheaper option.

options.text: Can I see the black one too?
options.feedback: Good. You compare options before deciding.

options.text: Thank you. Here is 7500 CFA.
options.feedback: You pay the exact amount and finish the purchase politely.

options.text: Can you give me a discount?
options.feedback: School supply prices are usually fixed. A big discount is not common.

options.text: I only have 7000 CFA. Can I remove one pen?
options.feedback: Smart adjustment. You change your order to match your money.

scenarios.title: Ordering Ndole at a Restaurant
scenarios.description: You go to a small restaurant in your neighborhood. You want to eat ndole.

start.text: Good afternoon! Welcome! What can I bring you?

options.text: Do you have ndole today?
options.feedback: Very clear. You ask directly for the dish you want.

options.text: I am hungry.
options.feedback: Tell the waiter what you want to eat, for example: “I would like ndole.”

options.text: What do you have?
options.feedback: It is better to ask first if they have the specific dish you want, like ndole.

step2.text: Yes, we have fresh ndole today. It is very good! Do you want it?

options.text: Yes, I want ndole. Is it spicy? Does it have meat?
options.feedback: Good. You accept the idea but still ask important questions.

options.text: Yes, bring it.
options.feedback: You should ask at least if it is spicy or what is inside before ordering.

options.text: How much does it cost?
options.feedback: Asking the price before ordering is also a good idea.

step3.text: The ndole is not very spicy, but it has a little pepper. It has beef and groundnuts. It is very delicious!

options.text: That sounds good! I will take ndole. How much is it?
options.feedback: Perfect. You decide and ask the price.

options.text: Does it have any other things?
options.feedback: The waiter already told you the main ingredients: beef and groundnuts. This is enough to decide.

options.text: Can you make it less spicy?
options.feedback: The waiter said it is not very spicy. You can try it as it is.

step4.text: One ndole is 2500 CFA. It comes with rice or cassava. Which one do you want?

options.text: I want ndole with rice, please. And bring me water too.
options.feedback: Clear order: main dish, side, and drink.

options.text: I want both rice and cassava.
options.feedback: The dish comes with one side: rice or cassava. You must choose one.

options.text: Is the price 2500 CFA with rice or with cassava?
options.feedback: Good clarification question about what is included in the price.

step5.text: Yes, 2500 CFA with rice or cassava. Now, what do you want to drink? We have water, juice, Coca-Cola, and beer.

options.text: I will drink water, please. Thank you.
options.feedback: Simple and polite drink order.

options.text: Bring me juice.
options.feedback: Say “please”, and you can also ask which juices they have.

options.text: What juice do you have?
options.feedback: Good. You ask for more information before choosing.

step6.text: We have mango juice and orange juice. Both are cold and fresh.

options.text: I want orange juice, please. How much is it?
options.feedback: Clear choice and good follow-up question about price.

options.text: Just bring water instead, please.
options.feedback: You change your mind politely to a simple drink.

options.text: Bring both juices.
options.feedback: Usually you only need one drink. Choose mango or orange.

step7.text: Okay! One ndole with rice and one orange juice. The juice is 500 CFA, so the total is 3000 CFA. I will bring your food soon.

options.text: Thank you. That is fine.
options.feedback: Polite and complete.

options.text: Okay, thank you.
options.feedback: Also a good polite response.

options.text: Can you hurry, I am very hungry?
options.feedback: If you want to ask this, say it politely, for example: “Please, can you bring it soon? I am very hungry.”

scenarios.title: Asking About Fufu in a Food Stand
scenarios.description: You go to a food stand in the morning. You want to eat fufu.

start.text: Good morning! You want to eat?

options.text: Good morning! Do you have fufu?
options.feedback: Polite and direct. You ask for the food you want.

options.text: Yes, I am hungry.
options.feedback: Say what you want to eat, for example: “Yes, I want to eat fufu.”

options.text: What do you have?
options.feedback: You can ask directly about fufu because many stands have it in the morning.

step2.text: Yes, I have very good fufu this morning. Fresh plantains from yesterday. Do you want it?

options.text: Yes! What comes with the fufu? Is there soup?
options.feedback: Good. You say yes and ask what is served with it.

options.text: Yes, give me fufu.
options.feedback: First ask what comes with the fufu, because there are different soups.

options.text: Is it expensive?
options.feedback: Ask what is included first, then ask the price.

step3.text: The fufu comes with two choices. One is egusi soup with meat and fish. The other is peanut soup with vegetables. Which one do you like?

options.text: What is in the egusi soup? Does it have a lot of meat?
options.feedback: Good questions to understand the ingredients.

options.text: I want the peanut soup.
options.feedback: You can choose, but it is useful to ask what is inside each soup before deciding.

options.text: Can I have both soups?
options.feedback: Normally you get one soup with the fufu. Having both usually costs extra.

step4.text: The egusi soup has good meat – beef and fish. It has pepper and spices. It is very tasty!

options.text: That sounds good! I will take fufu with egusi soup. How much is it?
options.feedback: Clear and polite decision with a price question.

options.text: Then give me the peanut soup instead.
options.feedback: It is okay to choose peanut soup, but you just asked about egusi. Decide once clearly after asking.

options.text: Is it very spicy?
options.feedback: She already said it has pepper and spices. Most Cameroonian food has some pepper. You can try it.

step5.text: The fufu with egusi soup is 1500 CFA. It is a big portion – you will be full!

options.text: Thank you! That is a good price. I will take it.
options.feedback: You accept the price politely.

options.text: That is too much! Make it 1000 CFA.
options.feedback: Street food prices are usually fixed. 1500 CFA is fair for a big portion.

options.text: Okay. Is the price the same if I choose peanut soup?
options.feedback: Good clarification about price and options.

step6.text: Yes, the price is the same. Let me put it in a plate for you. You want to eat here or take it home?

options.text: I will eat here, please. And bring me water.
options.feedback: Clear answer with a polite extra request.

options.text: Please put it in a package. I will eat at home.
options.feedback: Very polite and clear take-away request.

options.text: Eat here. No water, thank you.
options.feedback: Also fine. You clearly say your preference.

scenarios.title: Ordering Breakfast at a Small Shop
scenarios.description: You wake up late for school and you need to eat something quickly. You go to the small food shop near your house.

start.text: Good morning! You are late for school, no?

options.text: Yes, I am late! Do you have bread and eggs?
options.feedback: Good. You answer her and clearly ask for bread and eggs.

options.text: I want food.
options.feedback: This is too general. Say exactly what you want, for example: “I want bread and eggs.”

options.text: How much?
options.feedback: First say what you want to eat. After that, you can ask: “How much is it?”

step2.text: Yes, I have bread – white bread or brown bread. I have eggs – fried eggs or boiled eggs. And I have tea, coffee, or juice.

options.text: I want white bread, fried eggs, and tea, please.
options.feedback: Very clear order: you choose the type of bread, eggs, and drink, and you say “please”.

options.text: Give me bread and eggs.
options.feedback: Be more specific. Say which bread (white or brown) and which eggs (fried or boiled).

options.text: What is the cheapest?
options.feedback: First choose what you like. If money is a problem, then ask which option is cheaper.

step3.text: Good choice! The eggs will be ready in five minutes. The bread is already here, and the tea is fast.

options.text: That is fine. I have time. How much will everything cost?
options.feedback: Good. You accept the waiting time and ask politely about the total price.

options.text: I do not have five minutes. Make it faster!
options.feedback: Five minutes is already quick for breakfast. Be patient or find another place, but do not be rude.

options.text: Can I eat the bread while I wait for the eggs?
options.feedback: Nice idea. You can save time by eating the bread and drinking tea while the eggs are cooking.

step4.text: One white bread is 200 CFA, fried eggs are 400 CFA, and tea is 300 CFA. So everything is 900 CFA.

options.text: Okay, that is fine. Here is 1000 CFA. Keep the change.
options.feedback: Very polite. You pay more than the total and tell her to keep the change.

options.text: That is too much! Make it 500 CFA.
options.feedback: Prices in small shops are usually fixed and already fair. You cannot bargain like in a market.

options.text: Do I pay now or after I eat?
options.feedback: Good practical question. In many small shops, you pay after or while eating. It is fine to ask this clearly.

step5.text: Thank you! Eat quickly so you do not miss school. The bread and tea are here. The eggs are coming now.

options.text: Thank you for helping me! I will eat fast.
options.feedback: Polite and grateful. You show that you understand your situation.

options.text: The bread is not hot! Give me hot bread.
options.feedback: Bread is often not served hot. Do not complain about small things. Stay polite and eat.

options.text: Thank you so much! You are very kind.
options.feedback: Very positive and polite ending. Good use of “thank you”.

scenarios.title: Asking About Ingredients in a Dish
scenarios.description: You go to a food stand and you see a dish that looks good. But you are not sure what is in it.

start.text: Good afternoon! What do you want to eat today?

options.text: What do you have? I see something that looks good. What is it?
options.feedback: Good. You ask what the dish is before ordering it.

options.text: Give me that food.
options.feedback: First point to it or ask what it is: “What is this dish?” Then you can decide.

options.text: I do not like spicy food.
options.feedback: That is useful information, but first ask what the dish is and what is in it.

step2.text: This is couscous with fish and vegetables. It is very popular! Do you want to try it?

options.text: What is exactly in it? Is it very spicy? Does it have other meat besides fish?
options.feedback: Excellent. You ask about ingredients, spiciness, and other meat.

options.text: Yes, give me some.
options.feedback: You should ask about ingredients and spice level first, especially if you have allergies or do not like spicy food.

options.text: Is it expensive?
options.feedback: Price is important, but first check whether the dish is safe and suitable for you.

step3.text: The couscous has fish, carrots, onions, and tomatoes. It is seasoned with some pepper and spices, but it is not too spicy. Most people can eat it without problem.

options.text: Does it have chicken or beef also, or just fish?
options.feedback: Good follow-up question to confirm all the meat in the dish.

options.text: Okay, I will take it.
options.feedback: You said you do not like very spicy food and you have allergies. Make sure you understand all ingredients first.

options.text: Does it have groundnut? I am allergic to groundnut.
options.feedback: Very important allergy question. You should clearly say this before you decide.

step4.text: No chicken or beef – only fish. And there is no groundnut. Just the vegetables I told you and the spices. It is simple and healthy!

options.text: That sounds good! I will take it. But please do not make it very spicy, okay?
options.feedback: Good final decision. You order and also ask to reduce the spice.

options.text: No, I do not want it. Make me something without spice.
options.feedback: The seller said it is not very spicy and has no groundnut. You can still try it and ask for less pepper instead of refusing completely.

options.text: I am allergic to onions. Do you have another dish without onions?
options.feedback: Very important allergy information. Asking for another dish without onions is a good, safe choice.

step5.text: No problem! I will make it without much spice for you. It will be ready in ten minutes. It is 2000 CFA.

options.text: Thank you! That is perfect. How big is the portion? Will it fill me up?
options.feedback: Good polite questions about portion size.

options.text: That is too expensive!
options.feedback: 2000 CFA is a fair price for a dish with fish and vegetables. Complaining without a reason is not helpful.

options.text: Okay, I will wait. Thank you!
options.feedback: Polite and simple. You accept the price and waiting time.

scenarios.title: Complaining About Food That Is Not Good
scenarios.description: You ordered rice and sauce at a restaurant. When the food came, you noticed that the rice is cold and the sauce does not smell fresh.

start.text: Good afternoon! How is your food? Are you enjoying it?

options.text: Thank you for asking, but there is a problem. The rice is cold.
options.feedback: Very good. You are polite and you explain the problem clearly.

options.text: This food is bad!
options.feedback: Too general and sounds rude. Say exactly what is wrong, for example: “The rice is cold.”

options.text: I do not like it.
options.feedback: Explain why you do not like it: “The rice is cold and the sauce does not smell fresh.”

step2.text: Cold? Let me see... Oh, I am sorry about that. We were very busy in the kitchen. Do you want me to bring you hot rice?

options.text: Yes, please. And the sauce does not smell fresh. Can you change it too?
options.feedback: Excellent. You ask politely to change both the cold rice and the sauce.

options.text: No, never mind. I will eat this.
options.feedback: You paid for good food. If something is wrong, it is better to say it politely so they can fix it.

options.text: Yes, but make it fast!
options.feedback: The waiter is trying to help you. Be polite: “Yes, please. Thank you.”

step3.text: The sauce does not smell fresh? That is very strange. Let me check with the cook. Wait here, please.

options.text: Thank you. I appreciate your help.
options.feedback: Very polite. You show respect for the waiter’s effort.

options.text: Hurry! I am hungry.
options.feedback: The waiter is already helping you. Do not rush them; stay calm and polite.

options.text: Can I eat something else instead?
options.feedback: This is also a good solution. The waiter can ask the cook to change your dish to another one.

step4.text: I spoke with the cook. The sauce is okay, but I will bring you new hot rice and also a small extra portion of sauce. No charge for the extra. I am sorry for the problem.

options.text: That is very kind of you! Thank you for fixing this.
options.feedback: Excellent polite response. You accept the solution and show gratitude.

options.text: That is not enough. Give me money back.
options.feedback: The waiter is giving you new food and extra sauce for free. This is a fair solution; asking for money back now is too much.

options.text: Okay, thank you. I appreciate it.
options.feedback: Also polite and respectful. You accept the solution calmly.

scenarios.title: Paying and Tipping at a Restaurant
scenarios.description: You finished eating at a restaurant. Now you need to pay the bill and you are thinking about whether to leave a tip.

start.text: I hope you enjoyed your meal! Can I bring you anything else?

options.text: The food was excellent! Can I have the bill, please?
options.feedback: Very polite. You give a compliment and then ask for the bill.

options.text: I am finished. How much do I pay?
options.feedback: Add a thank-you and ask politely: “Thank you. Can I have the bill, please?”

options.text: Bring me the bill.
options.feedback: Sounds a bit direct. Say: “Please bring me the bill.”

step2.text: Of course! Let me bring the bill for you right away.

options.text: Thank you.
options.feedback: Short but polite.

options.text: Make it fast!
options.feedback: No need to rush the waiter. They are already bringing the bill.

options.text: How much is it?
options.feedback: Wait for the bill to arrive; then you can see and ask questions about it.

step3.text: Here is your bill. One rice and sauce is 2500 CFA, one juice is 500 CFA, and one bread is 300 CFA. The total is 3300 CFA.

options.text: Is that the total? And is the service charge included?
options.feedback: Good. You confirm the total and ask about service charge.

options.text: Okay, here is 3300 CFA.
options.feedback: It is useful to check the total and ask about service charge before paying.

options.text: That is too much! The food was not that good.
options.feedback: You already said the food was good. Complaining now is not honest or polite.

step4.text: Yes, that is the total. In this restaurant, we do not add service charge automatically. Some people give a small tip if the service was good, but it is not required.

options.text: You gave good service! I will give you a 300 CFA tip. Here is 3600 CFA.
options.feedback: Very kind and clear. You decide on a tip and include it in your payment.

options.text: I do not have extra money for a tip. Just take 3300 CFA.
options.feedback: This is fine. Tipping is not required in Cameroon if you do not have extra money.

options.text: What is a fair tip?
options.feedback: Good question if you are not sure how much to give.

step5.text: Thank you so much! Your tip is very kind. You are a good customer. Come back again!

options.text: You are welcome! Thank you for the good service. I will come back!
options.feedback: Very polite ending with thanks and future intention.

options.text: You are welcome.
options.feedback: Simple and polite.

options.text: Can you give me the change?
options.feedback: If you already decided to leave the extra as a tip, do not ask for change after that.

scenarios.title: Explaining a Headache to a Doctor
scenarios.description: You have had a bad headache for two days. You go to the doctor to get help.

start.text: Good morning! What is the problem? What brings you here today?

options.text: Good morning, doctor. I have had a bad headache for two days.
options.feedback: Very clear. You greet the doctor and say what the problem is and for how long.

options.text: I have a headache.
options.feedback: Also say how long you have had it: “I have had a headache for two days.”

options.text: My head hurts.
options.feedback: Correct, but incomplete. Add the duration: “My head has hurt for two days.”

step2.text: I see. A headache for two days. Where exactly does it hurt? Is it in the front, back, or all over?

options.text: It is in the front, between my eyes. And sometimes it is in the back also.
options.feedback: Very helpful detail about the location of the pain.

options.text: It hurts everywhere.
options.feedback: Try to be more specific: mostly front, back, or sides. The doctor needs more detail.

options.text: It hurts a lot!
options.feedback: You describe intensity, but the question is about location. Answer where it hurts.

step3.text: On a scale of one to ten, how bad is the pain? Is it light, medium, or very strong?

options.text: It is strong, like an 8. It makes it difficult for me to work.
options.feedback: Very clear answer with a number and an effect on your life.

options.text: It is bad.
options.feedback: Be more precise: for example, “It is about 8 out of 10.”

options.text: I do not know. Maybe 3?
options.feedback: You said it is a bad headache. 3 is a light pain. Try to give a number that matches how it really feels.

step4.text: I see. A strong headache. Do you have any other problems? Fever? Nausea? Sensitivity to light?

options.text: No fever or nausea, but yes, light hurts my eyes a little.
options.feedback: Good. You answer each part of the question.

options.text: No, just the headache.
options.feedback: If light hurts your eyes, tell the doctor. It is important information.

options.text: I do not understand. What is nausea?
options.feedback: Nausea means feeling like you will vomit. Answer if you feel that or not.

step5.text: Light sensitivity with this type of headache can mean many things. Have you been stressed? Did you sleep well last night? Did something change in your life?

options.text: Yes, I have been very stressed. I have exams next week, and I did not sleep well last night.
options.feedback: Very useful information about stress and sleep.

options.text: I do not know why I have a headache.
options.feedback: Think about stress, sleep, work, and changes. Try to give the doctor some ideas.

options.text: It is just a headache. Can you give me medicine?
options.feedback: Let the doctor finish asking questions so they can understand the problem before giving medicine.

step6.text: I understand. Stress and poor sleep can cause bad headaches like this. I will give you some pain medicine. Also, you need to rest more and reduce stress. Can you do that?

options.text: Yes, I will try to rest more. How do I take the medicine? How many times a day?
options.feedback: Good. You accept the advice and ask how to use the medicine correctly.

options.text: Okay, give me the medicine.
options.feedback: Before you accept, ask how to take it and how many times a day.

options.text: Will the medicine make me sleep?
options.feedback: This is a good question, but first ask about the basic instructions: dose and frequency.

step7.text: Take two tablets three times a day with food. Do not take it on an empty stomach. The side effects are small – maybe a little stomach upset. Drink lots of water, and come back in three days if the pain does not go away.

options.text: Thank you, doctor. I understand. Two tablets, three times a day with food. I will come back in three days if it does not get better.
options.feedback: Very good. You repeat the instructions to show you understand.

options.text: Can I take it whenever I want?
options.feedback: No. Follow the doctor’s instructions: two tablets, three times a day with food.

options.text: Okay, thank you!
options.feedback: Polite ending. Even better if you also repeat the instructions to remember them.

scenarios.title: Describing Stomach Pain at the Clinic
scenarios.description: You have had stomach pain since yesterday. You go to the clinic because you are worried.

start.text: Good afternoon! What is your problem today?

options.text: I have stomach pain since yesterday. I am very worried.
options.feedback: Very clear. You say what the problem is and how long it has lasted.

options.text: My stomach hurts.
options.feedback: This is good, but add the duration, for example: “My stomach has hurt since yesterday.”

options.text: I am sick.
options.feedback: Say what kind of sickness, for example: “I am sick. I have stomach pain since yesterday.”

step2.text: Stomach pain since yesterday. Is the pain everywhere in your stomach, or is it in one place?

options.text: It is mostly on the right side, below my ribs.
options.feedback: Very helpful. You give a clear location for the pain.

options.text: It is in my belly.
options.feedback: Try to be more exact: right side, left side, upper part, or lower part. This helps the nurse.

options.text: It comes and goes.
options.feedback: This describes how the pain behaves, but the nurse is asking where it is. Say the place first.

step3.text: Right side below the ribs. And the pain – is it constant, or does it come and go? When is it worse?

options.text: It is constant, but it gets worse when I eat. Right now it is very bad.
options.feedback: Excellent. You explain the pattern (constant) and what makes it worse (eating).

options.text: It hurts all the time.
options.feedback: Also say what makes it better or worse, especially when you eat or rest.

options.text: I do not know. It just hurts.
options.feedback: Try to notice if it changes after you eat, drink, or rest. The nurse needs this information.

step4.text: So the pain is worse when you eat. What did you eat before the pain started? And have you had bowel movements? Is the stool normal?

options.text: Yesterday I ate rice with fish and vegetables. I have had two bowel movements today, and the stool is a little soft.
options.feedback: Very clear. You say what you ate and describe how many times you went to the toilet and the stool type.

options.text: I ate normal food. And yes, I use the toilet.
options.feedback: Be more specific. Say what you ate and describe the stool (hard, soft, normal, watery).

options.text: I do not remember what I ate.
options.feedback: Try to remember if you ate fish, street food, or something unusual. It can help the nurse.

step5.text: I see. Soft stool after eating fish. Do you have fever? Are you vomiting or feeling nausea?

options.text: No fever, but I feel a little nausea. I did not vomit yet, but my stomach feels bad.
options.feedback: Good. You answer all parts of the question: fever, vomiting, and nausea.

options.text: No, I am fine.
options.feedback: You just said your stomach feels bad. Tell the nurse clearly if you feel nausea or not.

options.text: I feel very sick and maybe I will vomit.
options.feedback: Try to be clear: do you feel nausea now, or are you only afraid you might vomit later?

step6.text: Okay, I think you maybe ate something that was not fresh or did not agree with your stomach. Fish can sometimes do this. I will give you medicine to help your stomach, and you need to rest and drink water.

options.text: Thank you. What medicine? How do I take it? Can I eat now?
options.feedback: Good. You accept the plan and ask for instructions about the medicine and food.

options.text: Okay, I will go home.
options.feedback: Wait for the nurse to give you the medicine and explain how to take it before you leave.

options.text: Should I eat rice or something light?
options.feedback: The nurse will explain what you can eat. Listen to the full instructions first, then ask more questions if needed.

step7.text: This is medicine for stomach pain and to help digestion. Take it three times a day. For food, eat only light things – rice, bread, soup without meat, or bananas. No fish, no meat, no spicy food for two days. Drink plenty of water.

options.text: I understand. Light food for two days, and drink lots of water. What if the pain does not go away?
options.feedback: Very good. You repeat the instructions and ask what to do if it does not improve.

options.text: Can I eat fish again tomorrow?
options.feedback: The nurse said no fish or meat for two days. Wait until you feel better.

options.text: Thank you. I will do all of this.
options.feedback: Polite ending. You show that you will follow the advice.

scenarios.title: Asking About Medicine and Side Effects
scenarios.description: You go to the pharmacy to buy medicine for a cough. You want to understand everything about it before you buy it.

start.text: Good afternoon! What do you need?

options.text: I have a bad cough for three days. Can you give me medicine for it?
options.feedback: Very clear. You say what the problem is, how long it has lasted, and what you need.

options.text: I need cough medicine.
options.feedback: Add how long you have had the cough, for example: “I need cough medicine. I have been coughing for three days.”

options.text: I am coughing.
options.feedback: Say clearly what you want: “I am coughing. I need medicine for my cough.”

step2.text: I have a very good cough medicine. It is a syrup that stops coughing and helps you breathe better. Many people use it and they are happy.

options.text: Thank you. What is exactly in this medicine? Does it have any side effects?
options.feedback: Excellent. You ask about ingredients and side effects before buying.

options.text: How much is it?
options.feedback: First learn what the medicine does and if it is safe. Then ask the price.

options.text: Is it safe?
options.feedback: This is a good question. Make it stronger by also asking what is in it and what side effects there are.

step3.text: This syrup has honey and herbs. It is natural and very safe. It coats your throat and stops the cough reflex. You will feel better quickly, usually within two days.

options.text: That sounds good. Are there any side effects? Can I take it with other medicine?
options.feedback: Very good. You ask about side effects and if it mixes safely with other medicine.

options.text: Okay, give me the medicine.
options.feedback: Before you buy it, ask about side effects and if it is okay with other medicine you take.

options.text: Will it make me sleep?
options.feedback: This is one possible side effect, but first ask about side effects in general.

step4.text: Side effects are rare because it is natural. Some people may have a little stomach upset or allergic reaction, but this is very rare. If you take other medicine, this syrup is usually okay with everything. But if you are taking blood pressure medicine, tell me now.

options.text: No, I am not taking any other medicine. So it is safe for me?
options.feedback: Good. You answer and confirm that it is safe in your case.

options.text: What if I have allergic reaction?
options.feedback: Serious allergy is very rare. If you notice any problem, stop taking it and come back or see a doctor. The pharmacist already explained this is rare.

options.text: I do not know if I am taking blood pressure medicine.
options.feedback: Think about your regular tablets. If you have high blood pressure and take daily medicine, tell the pharmacist.

step5.text: Yes, it is safe. Now, how to take it: take two spoons three times a day. Take it after eating food, not on an empty stomach. Finish the bottle – about five days of medicine.

options.text: Two spoons, three times a day, after eating. I will take it for five days. How much does it cost?
options.feedback: Very good. You repeat the instructions to show you understand, then ask the price.

options.text: Can I take more to get better faster?
options.feedback: No. Do not take more than the dose. It will not make you better faster and can cause problems.

options.text: What if I forget to take it?
options.feedback: If you forget a dose, take it when you remember, but try to keep the three-times-a-day schedule. The main idea is to follow the instructions regularly.

step6.text: The bottle is 2500 CFA. If your cough does not go away after five days, come back and see a doctor. Do not wait too long.

options.text: Okay, here is 2500 CFA. Thank you for explaining everything.
options.feedback: Polite and clear. You pay and show appreciation for the explanation.

options.text: That is expensive! Can you reduce it?
options.feedback: Pharmacy prices are fixed. 2500 CFA is a normal price for this kind of syrup.

options.text: Thank you. I will come back if it does not get better.
options.feedback: Good. You accept the advice and know when to return.

scenarios.title: Explaining an Illness to a Pharmacist
scenarios.description: You have been feeling weak and tired for a week. You go to the pharmacy without seeing a doctor first.

start.text: Good morning! What can I help you with?

options.text: I have been feeling weak and tired for a week. I do not know what is wrong.
options.feedback: Very clear description of both feeling and duration.

options.text: I do not feel good.
options.feedback: Say exactly how you feel, for example: “I feel weak and tired.”

options.text: Can you give me medicine?
options.feedback: First describe your problem. Then the pharmacist can decide if medicine is needed.

step2.text: I see. Weak and tired for a week. When did this start? Was it sudden or did it come slowly?

options.text: It came slowly. Last week I felt a little tired, and now it is worse. I do not have energy for anything.
options.feedback: Good. You describe how it started and that it is getting worse.

options.text: I woke up tired one day.
options.feedback: This tells when it began, but also say if it is getting better or worse.

options.text: I do not know when it started.
options.feedback: Try to remember the last time you felt normal. That helps the pharmacist understand.

step3.text: Getting worse, I see. Do you have fever? Any pain in your body? Are you eating normally?

options.text: No fever, but my body feels heavy. I am eating, but I do not feel hungry. My appetite is small.
options.feedback: Very helpful information about fever, body feeling, and appetite.

options.text: I feel bad everywhere.
options.feedback: Be more precise. Say if you have headache, chest pain, stomach pain, or joint pain.

options.text: I cannot eat.
options.feedback: Explain more: you cannot eat at all, or you just do not feel hungry? This difference is important.

step4.text: Heavy body, no fever, small appetite. Are you sleeping? Do you sleep normally, or do you have trouble sleeping? And do you have any other symptoms – cough, sore throat, anything?

options.text: I am sleeping too much – I sleep at least ten hours every night and I am still tired. No cough or sore throat. Just weak.
options.feedback: Clear description of sleep pattern and other symptoms.

options.text: I sleep a normal amount.
options.feedback: You said you are very tired. If you sleep more than usual, tell the pharmacist that.

options.text: I do not sleep well.
options.feedback: Explain how: you cannot fall asleep, you wake up many times, or you sleep too much.

step5.text: Sleeping too much and still tired, no fever, no other symptoms, appetite is small… This can be many things – maybe you are stressed, maybe you need iron or vitamins, or maybe something else. I think you should see a doctor first, before taking medicine from me.

options.text: Really? Is it very serious? Should I go today?
options.feedback: Good follow-up question. You check how urgent it is.

options.text: No, just give me vitamin medicine.
options.feedback: Without knowing the real cause, vitamins alone may not help. The pharmacist advises you to see a doctor first.

options.text: Can you give me something to help me?
options.feedback: The safest “something” is after a doctor checks you. That is why the pharmacist wants you to go to a clinic.

step6.text: It may not be very serious, but it is better to know. Go to a clinic and explain these symptoms. The doctor will check you and maybe take blood. Then you will know what is wrong and we can give you the right medicine.

options.text: Thank you for telling me. I will go to the clinic today. Do you know a good clinic near here?
options.feedback: Very good. You accept the advice and ask for a recommendation.

options.text: Okay, I will go tomorrow.
options.feedback: You have felt like this for a week already. Going today is better if you can.

options.text: Thank you for your help. I understand.
options.feedback: Polite ending. You show that you accept the plan.

scenarios.title: Asking About Opening Hours at the Health Center
scenarios.description: You need to go to the health center because you are not feeling well. You do not know the opening hours.

start.text: Good afternoon! Can I help you?

options.text: Yes, what are your opening hours? I need to come see a doctor tomorrow.
options.feedback: Good. You ask for the schedule and explain why you need it.

options.text: I want to see a doctor.
options.feedback: This is true, but first ask when the health center is open and if you can come tomorrow.

options.text: Are you open?
options.feedback: Ask for the full schedule, for example: “What time do you open and close?”

step2.text: We open at 7 AM and close at 5 PM, Monday to Friday. On Saturday we open at 8 AM and close at 1 PM. We are closed on Sunday.

options.text: So you open at 7 AM on weekdays, and 8 AM on Saturday. Do I need to come early, or can I come anytime during the day?
options.feedback: Very good. You repeat the key information and ask about the best time to come.

options.text: Can I come tomorrow?
options.feedback: You now know the hours. Ask if you should come early or if you need an appointment.

options.text: That is late! Can you open earlier?
options.feedback: The opening hours are fixed. You need to plan your visit within these times.

step3.text: You can come anytime, but if you come early in the morning, there is a shorter wait. Many people come before 9 AM. Do you need an appointment, or do you have an emergency?

options.text: I do not have an emergency, but I am not feeling well. Do I need to call for an appointment first?
options.feedback: Good. You explain your situation and ask clearly about appointments.

options.text: I will just come whenever.
options.feedback: It is better to know if you must call first or if walk-ins are accepted. Ask clearly.

options.text: I have an emergency right now!
options.feedback: Real emergencies are usually handled at a hospital or emergency service, not a normal health center.

step4.text: You do not need an appointment. You can come without calling first. Just come in the morning if you can, and it will be faster. Bring your ID card and any money you have – not all services are free here.

options.text: Thank you! So I can come tomorrow morning with my ID card. What time should I come?
options.feedback: Very clear. You repeat the main points and ask for a more specific time range.

options.text: How much does it cost?
options.feedback: Costs depend on what the doctor does. You can ask more about that when you arrive.

options.text: Do I need to bring my whole family?
options.feedback: The receptionist is talking about your visit. You only need to bring yourself (unless your family also needs care).

step5.text: Yes, come anytime between 7 AM and 12 PM tomorrow for the shortest wait. Have your symptoms ready to explain to the doctor. What is wrong with you?

options.text: I have been having stomach pain and fever for two days.
options.feedback: Good. You give a short, clear description of your main symptoms.

options.text: I am not sure what is wrong. The doctor will tell me.
options.feedback: Even if you are not sure, describe your main symptoms now (pain, fever, cough, etc.).

options.text: I will tell the doctor when I come.
options.feedback: This is also acceptable. The doctor will ask for details during the visit.

scenarios.title: Asking a Teacher for Help with Homework
scenarios.description: You have English homework but you do not understand some of the questions. You go to see your English teacher after class.

start.text: Hello! Do you want to talk to me about something?

options.text: Yes, thank you. Can you help me with my English homework? I do not understand some questions.
options.feedback: Very polite and clear. You say what you need and why.

options.text: I have homework questions.
options.feedback: Be more polite and clear, for example: “Can you help me with my homework questions?”

options.text: This is too difficult!
options.feedback: Say what is difficult and ask for help: “This homework is difficult. Can you explain some questions?”

step2.text: Of course! I can help you. Show me your homework. What questions do you not understand?

options.text: Thank you, teacher. I do not understand question three and five. Can you explain them to me?
options.feedback: Very good. You are specific about which questions you need help with.

options.text: All of it.
options.feedback: Try to point to specific questions, for example: “Questions three and five are difficult for me.”

options.text: Can you just give me the answers?
options.feedback: The teacher wants you to learn. Ask for explanations, not only answers.

step3.text: Okay, look at question three. It asks you to change this sentence from present to past tense. What is the original sentence?

options.text: The original sentence is 'I am eating dinner.' Should I write 'I was eating dinner'?
options.feedback: Excellent. You read the sentence and try to change it yourself.

options.text: I do not know.
options.feedback: Look at your exercise and read the sentence aloud. Then try to answer.

options.text: Just tell me the answer.
options.feedback: Try first. The teacher can correct you and explain, which helps you learn.

step4.text: Good! Yes, 'I was eating dinner' is correct. Do you understand the pattern? When you change 'am' to past, it becomes 'was'. Do you see other verbs like this in the homework?

options.text: I see! So 'you are playing' becomes 'you were playing'. Is that right?
options.feedback: Very good. You apply the pattern to another example.

options.text: I do not know. Can you give me more answers?
options.feedback: Use the rule the teacher gave you to try other sentences yourself.

options.text: This is still confusing.
options.feedback: Try one more example using the pattern. Then ask which part is still confusing.

step5.text: Exactly! You understand now. Try to do the rest of question three by yourself using this pattern. Then show me. If you are correct, you will understand question five too, because it is the same pattern.

options.text: Thank you, teacher! I will try it now. Can I ask you if I need more help?
options.feedback: Very good. You show independence but also know you can ask again.

options.text: Okay, but please stay with me while I do it.
options.feedback: The teacher wants you to practice alone first. You can ask again if you get stuck.

options.text: Thank you for helping me. I understand now.
options.feedback: Polite ending. You show that the explanation helped you.

scenarios.title: Explaining Why You Were Absent from School
scenarios.description: You were absent from school yesterday because you were sick. Today you come to school and your teacher asks where you were.

start.text: Good morning. I noticed you were absent yesterday. Where were you? Do you have a note from your parents?

options.text: Good morning, teacher. I was sick yesterday, so I could not come to school. I have a note from my mother here.
options.feedback: Very clear. You explain the reason and show the note.

options.text: I was not here yesterday.
options.feedback: The teacher knows you were not here. Say why you were absent.

options.text: I was busy.
options.feedback: “Busy” is not a good reason. Say the real reason, for example, that you were sick.

step2.text: I see. Let me read your mother's note. It says you had a fever. Is that correct? Are you better now?

options.text: Yes, I had fever and a sore throat. I am much better today, thank you for asking.
options.feedback: Good. You confirm the information and show politeness.

options.text: Yes, I am okay now.
options.feedback: This is fine, but add what kind of sickness you had and thank the teacher.

options.text: A little. I still feel tired.
options.feedback: Also correct. If you still feel tired, tell the teacher honestly.

step3.text: Thank you for telling me. When you are absent, it is important to let the school know. Did your parents call the school or only send this note?

options.text: They only sent the note. I am sorry I was absent yesterday.
options.feedback: You apologize and answer the question. This is polite and responsible.

options.text: I do not know.
options.feedback: Try to ask your parents in the future. The school must know why you are absent.

options.text: It is not important.
options.feedback: It is important. The school must record all absences and reasons.

step4.text: I understand. I am happy you are back. But you missed lessons from yesterday. We studied past tense verbs and we started a short writing exercise. Do you know what we did?

options.text: No, I do not know what you studied. Can you tell me what I need to do to catch up?
options.feedback: Very good. You ask directly how to catch up.

options.text: I will study tonight.
options.feedback: That is good, but first ask what exactly you missed so you know what to study.

options.text: I will ask my friends.
options.feedback: You can ask friends, but the teacher can give you clear instructions now.

step5.text: We did a worksheet on past tense, and the class wrote a short paragraph about 'What I did yesterday'. Here is the worksheet from yesterday, and here is the writing task.

options.text: Thank you, teacher. When do I need to finish the worksheet and the paragraph?
options.feedback: Excellent. You ask about the deadline so you can plan your work.

options.text: This is too much work!
options.feedback: Do not complain. This work helps you catch up with the class.

options.text: I will do it sometime.
options.feedback: Be more specific. Ask when it is due and plan to do it soon.

step6.text: Please finish both for tomorrow. If you are ever sick again, ask your parents to call the school, and when you return, come to me directly so I can give you the work you missed. Do you understand?

options.text: Yes, I understand. I will finish the work for tomorrow, and next time I am sick, we will call the school. Thank you for helping me catch up.
options.feedback: Very good. You show responsibility for both the homework and future absences.

options.text: Okay, I will see what I can do.
options.feedback: Be clear and serious. Promise to finish the work and follow the rules.

options.text: I will only do the worksheet.
options.feedback: The teacher gave you two tasks. You need to do both.

scenarios.title: Asking About Grades or Test Results
scenarios.description: Your teacher gave back test papers today. You are worried about your grade and want to ask the teacher about it.

start.text: Here are your test papers back. Look at your grades.

options.text: Thank you, teacher. I have a question about my grade. Can I ask you?
options.feedback: Polite and clear. You ask permission first.

options.text: Why is my grade so low?
options.feedback: You can ask this, but be more polite first: “Can I ask you about my grade?”

options.text: This is not fair!
options.feedback: Do not complain immediately. Ask for an explanation calmly.

step2.text: Of course. What is your question about your grade?

options.text: I studied very hard for this test, but my grade is only 12/20. Can you explain what was wrong?
options.feedback: Very good. You explain your effort and ask for clarification.

options.text: My grade is not good.
options.feedback: Be specific. Ask what answers were wrong or what you did not understand.

options.text: Can you give me more marks?
options.feedback: Do not ask for extra marks. Ask how you can improve instead.

step3.text: You got 12 out of 20. Let me show you: the first five questions are correct. But questions six and seven, you did not explain your answers. And in question eight, you used the wrong verb tense.

options.text: I see. So I need to explain my answers, not just give short answers. And I need to be careful with verb tenses. Can I study these areas and try again?
options.feedback: Excellent summary of the problem and a positive request.

options.text: But I do not understand verb tenses.
options.feedback: That is okay, but now ask the teacher to help you practice them.

options.text: These questions were too hard!
options.feedback: Other students answered them. Focus on understanding, not complaining.

step4.text: Yes, you can study and we can do extra practice. I cannot change this test grade, but I can give you another small quiz next week. If you do well, it will help your overall mark. Would you like that?

options.text: Yes, thank you. I would like another quiz. Can you also give me extra exercises on verb tenses to practice at home?
options.feedback: Very good. You accept the opportunity and ask for practice.

options.text: If I do the quiz, will you forget this grade?
options.feedback: The grade stays, but the new quiz can improve your average.

options.text: No, I do not want another test.
options.feedback: This is a chance to improve. Refusing will not help your grade.

step5.text: I will prepare some verb tense exercises for you. You can take them home today and bring them back on Friday. We will review your answers together before the quiz.
