options.text: That is very helpful. I will do all the exercises and bring them on Friday. Can you show me one example now so I do it correctly?
options.feedback: Excellent. You confirm the plan and ask for a model.

options.text: Friday is too soon.
options.feedback: You have enough time if you start early. Use the time well.

options.text: I will try to do some of them.
options.feedback: Try to do all the exercises. They are for your benefit.

step6.text: Here is an example: ‘I go to school’ becomes ‘I went to school’. Follow the pattern in the exercises. I am happy you asked about your grade. This is how you improve.

options.text: Thank you, teacher. I understand the example. I will work hard and bring everything on Friday.
options.feedback: Very good. You show determination to improve.

options.text: Okay, I will see what happens.
options.feedback: Show a clear decision to work hard, not a passive attitude.

options.text: Thank you for explaining my mistakes. I feel better now.
options.feedback: Good. You appreciate the feedback.

scenarios.title: Requesting Extra Lessons for a Difficult Subject
scenarios.description: Mathematics is very difficult for you. You want to ask your math teacher if you can have extra lessons after school.

start.text: Hello! Do you want to talk to me?

options.text: Yes, please. I have a problem with mathematics. Can I ask for your help?
options.feedback: Very polite and clear. You state your need for help.

options.text: I do not understand math.
options.feedback: Also say you want help and ask if the teacher can give extra lessons.

options.text: I need to pass this subject.
options.feedback: Explain that you want extra support, not only that you must pass.

step2.text: Of course I can help. What is the problem? What do you not understand in mathematics?

options.text: I find fractions and percentages very difficult. I do not understand how to solve problems with them. Can you give me extra lessons?
options.feedback: Good. You specify the difficult topics and ask for extra lessons.

options.text: Everything is hard.
options.feedback: Be specific. Name the topics: fractions, percentages, equations, etc.

options.text: I am not good at math.
options.feedback: Say exactly which parts you do not understand.

step3.text: Fractions and percentages are important topics. Yes, I can give you extra lessons. When are you free? After school, or on another day?

options.text: Can I come on Tuesday and Thursday after school? I finish at 3 PM, and I can come at 3:30 PM. Is that okay?
options.feedback: Excellent. You propose specific times that work for you.

options.text: I do not know when I am free.
options.feedback: Think about your timetable and suggest specific times.

options.text: Can we do it during lunch?
options.feedback: Lunch is short. After school is better for longer lessons.

step4.text: Tuesday and Thursday at 3:30 PM is good for me. Each lesson will be one hour. We will start with fractions, then percentages. You need to bring a notebook, your math book, and a pen.

options.text: Thank you, teacher. That is perfect. I will bring everything. Do we start this week?
options.feedback: Very good. You confirm the details and ask about the start date.

options.text: One hour is too long.
options.feedback: One hour gives enough time to learn and practice.

options.text: Okay, thank you.
options.feedback: Ask when the lessons begin so you do not miss them.

step5.text: Yes, we start this Tuesday. Also, I will give you a little homework after each extra lesson. It is important that you practice at home. Will you be able to do that?

options.text: Yes, I will do the homework after each lesson. I really want to improve my math.
options.feedback: Great attitude. You commit to doing the necessary work.

options.text: Maybe. I am not sure.
options.feedback: Be serious. Extra lessons only help if you also do the practice.

options.text: I do not like homework.
options.feedback: Homework is part of learning. You need it to get better.

step6.text: Good. Please tell your parents about these extra lessons so they know where you are after school. If you cannot come one day, tell me in advance.

options.text: I will tell my parents today. Thank you very much for helping me. I will see you on Tuesday at 3:30.
options.feedback: Perfect ending. You confirm communication with parents and the next meeting.

options.text: If I forget to come, it is not a problem.
options.feedback: It is a problem. Always inform the teacher if you must miss a lesson.

options.text: Okay, but I will come only when I feel like it.
options.feedback: Extra lessons require regular attendance to be useful.

scenarios.title: Reporting Bullying to a Teacher
scenarios.description: Another student has been bullying you. You decide to tell your teacher because it is getting worse.

start.text: Good afternoon. You look worried. Is something wrong?

options.text: Yes, teacher. I have a big problem. Can I talk to you about it?
options.feedback: Good. You ask for permission to discuss a serious issue.

options.text: Nothing is wrong.
options.feedback: The teacher can see you are upset. It is better to tell them.

options.text: A student is bothering me.
options.feedback: This is true, but you need to ask if you can explain it fully.

step2.text: Yes, of course. You can talk to me. Tell me what happened. What is the problem?

options.text: A student in my class keeps saying mean things to me – calling me names and telling other students not to talk to me. Yesterday, they took my pen and did not give it back.
options.feedback: Very clear. You describe the specific bullying behaviors.

options.text: They do not like me.
options.feedback: Give details: what do they say, what do they do?

options.text: They are always rude.
options.feedback: Give specific examples so the teacher understands the situation.

step3.text: That is very wrong. I am sorry this is happening to you. How long has this been going on? Does it happen every day? How do you feel about it?

options.text: It started about three weeks ago. At first it was just words, but now it is worse. It happens almost every day, and I feel very sad and worried. Sometimes I do not want to come to school.
options.feedback: Excellent. You explain the duration, frequency, and emotional impact.

options.text: It happens sometimes.
options.feedback: The teacher needs to know how often. Explain clearly: every day, a few times a week, etc.

options.text: I feel bad.
options.feedback: Say more: sad, scared, worried, angry. This helps the teacher understand the impact.

step4.text: I understand. This is bullying, and it is not acceptable. Do other students see this happen? And do you feel safe in the classroom and in the playground?

options.text: Yes, other students see it, but they are scared to say anything. Sometimes my friend talks to me, but they keep quiet because they are worried. I do not feel safe when that student is near me.
options.feedback: Very brave and honest. You explain the social situation and your safety concerns.

options.text: Nobody knows.
options.feedback: If it happens in class or in the yard, other students probably see it. Tell the truth.

options.text: I am safe. It is nothing.
options.feedback: You already said you are worried and do not want to come to school. Be honest.

step5.text: Thank you for telling me all this. You did the right thing. I will talk to this student privately and also speak to the class about bullying. I will ask another teacher to help me watch the situation. I also want to change where you sit so you are not next to this student.

options.text: Thank you, teacher. I feel better knowing you will act. Changing my seat is a good idea.
options.feedback: Good. You acknowledge the teacher's plan and support.

options.text: I do not want any change.
options.feedback: Small changes, like seating, can help keep you safe and comfortable.

options.text: Can you shout at the student in front of the class?
options.feedback: The teacher will choose the best way to handle it. Public shouting may not help.

step6.text: If this happens again, come tell me immediately. You can also tell your parents what is happening so they know. I will write down what you told me today so we can follow up. You are not alone.

options.text: Thank you, teacher. I will tell my parents tonight, and if it happens again, I will come to you right away.
options.feedback: Very good. You agree to keep communicating and seeking help.

options.text: I will keep it to myself.
options.feedback: Do not keep bullying secret. Adults can help protect you.

options.text: Thank you. I was very worried before, but now I feel safer.
options.feedback: Good. You express relief and trust in the teacher.

scenarios.title: Asking for a Deadline Extension
scenarios.description: You have a project due tomorrow, but you got sick this week and you did not finish it. You need to ask your teacher for more time.

start.text: Do you have your project for me today?

options.text: No, teacher. I have a problem. Can I ask for your help?
options.feedback: Good. You admit you don't have it and ask to explain.

options.text: I do not have it.
options.feedback: Say why you do not have it and ask for more time.

options.text: I was busy.
options.feedback: “Busy” is not a good reason. Explain the real problem.

step2.text: What is the problem? Why do you not have your project?

options.text: I was very sick all this week. I went to the clinic on Monday and I could not do my project. I am better now, but I only started the work yesterday. Can I have a few more days to finish it?
options.feedback: Very clear. You explain the sickness, your current progress, and your request.

options.text: I forgot about it.
options.feedback: This is not true if you were sick and knew about the project. Be honest.

options.text: Can I just give you half of it?
options.feedback: Do not offer incomplete work. Ask for an extension to finish properly.

step3.text: I see you were sick. That is difficult. Did you get a note from your parents or from the clinic? And what have you finished so far?

options.text: Yes, my mother wrote a note, and the clinic gave me a paper. I can bring them tomorrow. I have finished the first two pages and the outline for the rest.
options.feedback: Excellent. You offer proof and show that you have started the work.

options.text: No, I do not have any note, and I did not start anything.
options.feedback: If possible, bring proof of sickness and at least start some work.

options.text: I do not want to show anything yet.
options.feedback: Showing what you have done helps the teacher trust you.

step4.text: Thank you for explaining. That helps. How many more days do you think you need to complete the project fully?

options.text: I need three more days. I can give you the complete project on Friday. I will work every evening until then.
options.feedback: Reasonable request. You set a specific deadline and commit to working hard.

options.text: I need one week.
options.feedback: One week is long. Ask for a reasonable number of days, like two or three.

options.text: I am not sure. Maybe many days.
options.feedback: Be specific so the teacher can decide clearly.

step5.text: All right. I will give you until Friday. This extension is because you were sick and you already started the project. Next time, please tell me as soon as you know you have a problem. Do you understand?

options.text: Yes, I understand, teacher. Next time I will tell you immediately if I am sick or have a problem. Thank you for giving me until Friday.
options.feedback: Very good. You acknowledge the condition and thank the teacher.

options.text: Okay, but can you give me until next week instead?
options.feedback: You already agreed on Friday. Do not ask for more without a serious reason.

options.text: Thank you, but I still think one week is better.
options.feedback: The teacher has already made a fair decision.

step6.text: Good. Make a plan: work a little each day. If you have any questions while you work, you can ask me after class. I want you to learn from this project, not just finish it.

options.text: Thank you, teacher. I will plan my time and work on it every day until Friday. If I have questions, I will come to you.
options.feedback: Perfect ending. You show responsibility and a good work ethic.

options.text: I will do everything on Thursday night.
options.feedback: Last-minute work is stressful and usually not good quality. Use the extra days well.

options.text: Okay, I will see.
options.feedback: Be clear and serious about your plan to finish on time.

scenarios.title: Explaining School Rules to a New Student
scenarios.description: A new student just arrived at your school today. You help them understand the rules and how things work.

start.text: Hello. This is my first day. I am very nervous. Can you help me?

options.text: Yes, of course! I am happy to help you. What do you want to know about the school?
options.feedback: Very welcoming. You show that you are ready to help.

options.text: Yes, follow me.
options.feedback: That is okay, but first ask what they want to know so you can answer their questions.

options.text: The rules are complicated.
options.feedback: This can make them more nervous. Be positive and encouraging.

step2.text: Thank you. I want to know about the school rules. What time does school start? And what do I need to bring?

options.text: School starts at 7:30 AM every morning. You must come on time. You need to bring notebooks, pens, and your schoolbag. Some days you also need your sports clothes.
options.feedback: Good. You provide clear information about time and materials.

options.text: I do not know. Ask the teacher.
options.feedback: You know these things. Answer with the basic information.

options.text: You need everything.
options.feedback: This is not clear. Say exactly what they must bring.

step3.text: Okay, I understand. What about the school day? When do we have break? When does school finish?

options.text: We start at 7:30 AM, then we have a short break at 10 AM and a longer break for lunch at 12:30 PM. The school day ends at 3 PM.
options.feedback: Excellent. You explain the schedule clearly.

options.text: We have breaks sometimes.
options.feedback: Be specific about break times and when school ends.

options.text: You will see the timetable in class.
options.feedback: The timetable is helpful, but you can already explain the basic times.

step4.text: Thank you. I understand the times now. What about the rules? What am I allowed to do, and what am I not allowed to do?

options.text: We have several rules. You must listen to teachers and be respectful. You cannot use a phone in class – it is not allowed. You cannot talk when the teacher is talking. You must wear your school uniform every day. And you cannot run in the corridors – you must walk.
options.feedback: Very thorough. You cover the most important rules.

options.text: There are many rules. You will learn them.
options.feedback: Tell them the most important rules now so they do not break them by mistake.

options.text: Just do what everyone else does.
options.feedback: The new student needs clear rules, not only to copy others.

step5.text: I understand. What happens if I break a rule? Is the punishment very bad?

options.text: Do not worry too much. If you make a small mistake, the teacher will just warn you. If you break a serious rule many times, the teacher may call your parents or give you detention. Just try to follow the rules and you will be fine.
options.feedback: Good. You explain the consequences realistically without scaring them.

options.text: Yes, it is very bad. You will be punished.
options.feedback: This can scare them. Explain calmly and honestly without making it sound terrible.

options.text: I do not know. Ask the principal.
options.feedback: You know the basic consequences. Share them to help the new student.

step6.text: Okay, I feel a bit better now. What if I forget a rule or get confused in class?

options.text: That is normal on your first days. If you are not sure about something, you can ask the teacher or ask me quietly. We will help you. You are not alone.
options.feedback: Very supportive. You reassure them and offer help.

options.text: You must not forget any rule.
options.feedback: Everyone forgets sometimes. Be kind and realistic.

options.text: Just be quiet and do not ask questions.
options.feedback: Asking questions is important. Do not tell them to stay silent.

step7.text: Thank you for explaining everything. I feel less nervous now. Will you be my friend?

options.text: Of course! I will be your friend. Welcome to our school! If you have more questions, you can ask me anytime. We can also sit together at lunch if you want.
options.feedback: Perfect ending. You welcome the new student and offer friendship.

options.text: Maybe.
options.feedback: Be welcoming and kind. The new student needs support.

options.text: Yes, let us sit together at lunch.
options.feedback: Good. You accept the friendship.

scenarios.title: Greeting an Elder When You Arrive Home
scenarios.description: You come home from school and your uncle is visiting. You need to greet him respectfully.

start.text: Good afternoon! Is that you coming home from school?

options.text: Good afternoon, Uncle. How are you today?
options.feedback: Very polite. You use the correct title and ask about his well-being.

options.text: Hi, what are you doing here?
options.feedback: Too casual. Greet your uncle respectfully first.

options.text: I am home.
options.feedback: This sounds rude. Use a polite greeting.

step2.text: I am fine, thank you. How are you? How was school today?

options.text: I am fine, thank you for asking. School was good. I learned many new things today.
options.feedback: Good. You answer politely and share a positive detail.

options.text: School was okay.
options.feedback: Give a little more information. It shows respect and interest.

options.text: Tired.
options.feedback: First say "I am fine, thank you", then you can say you are tired.

step3.text: That is good. Which subjects did you have today? Did you enjoy them?

options.text: Today we had English, mathematics, and science. I enjoyed English and mathematics. Science was a little difficult, but I tried my best.
options.feedback: Excellent. You give specific details about your subjects.

options.text: Many subjects.
options.feedback: Be specific. Your uncle wants to hear details about your day.

options.text: I do not remember.
options.feedback: Try to remember at least some subjects you studied.

step4.text: I am happy you are trying. And at home, are you helping your parents? Do you respect them and do your chores?

options.text: Yes, Uncle. I try to help my parents. I sweep the floor, wash dishes sometimes, and I listen when they speak to me.
options.feedback: Very good. You list specific ways you help and show respect.

options.text: Sometimes I help.
options.feedback: Show clear responsibility. Mention what you actually do to help.

options.text: No, I am too tired to help.
options.feedback: This shows disrespect. Elders expect you to help your family.

step5.text: That is good. A child must respect parents and help at home. You said science is a bit difficult. If you need help with science, tell me. I studied science in my time.

options.text: Thank you very much, Uncle! I appreciate your help. If I find something difficult in science, I will ask you. You are very kind.
options.feedback: Polite and grateful. You accept the offer of help.

options.text: Okay, maybe.
options.feedback: Show more gratitude and respect. He is offering his time.

options.text: I will ask my teacher only.
options.feedback: You can ask both your teacher and your uncle. Accept his kindness.

step6.text: Good. Now go change your uniform and rest a little. School is tiring. Your mother is in the kitchen. Go greet her too.

options.text: Yes, Uncle. Thank you for the advice. I will change my clothes and greet Mama now. It was nice to see you.
options.feedback: Perfect ending. You show respect and follow instructions.

options.text: Okay, bye.
options.feedback: Say a proper goodbye and show respect in your words.

options.text: Thank you, Uncle. See you later.
options.feedback: Good. You end the conversation politely.

scenarios.title: Asking Permission to Go Out with Friends
scenarios.description: Your friends invited you to play football. You need to ask your mother's permission.

start.text: You are home from school early. What do you want?

options.text: Good afternoon, Mama. Can I ask you something, please?
options.feedback: Polite start. You greet your mother and ask for attention.

options.text: Mama, my friends want to play.
options.feedback: Greet your mother politely and ask permission clearly.

options.text: Can I go out?
options.feedback: First greet your mother and then explain your plan.

step2.text: Yes, what do you want to ask me?

options.text: My friends invited me to play football at the field this afternoon. Can I go, please? I will be back home before 5 PM.
options.feedback: Very clear. You state the activity, location, and return time.

options.text: I want to go play.
options.feedback: Say where, with whom, and when you will return.

options.text: Can I go with my friends to the field?
options.feedback: That is the main question, but add the time you will come back.

step3.text: Football at the field. Who are these friends? Will you be safe there?

options.text: Yes, Mama. My friends from school – James, Joseph, and Michael. We always play together. The field is near the school, and there are many people around, so it is safe.
options.feedback: Good. You identify your friends and explain why the location is safe.

options.text: Yes, it is safe.
options.feedback: Give names and reasons why you think it is safe.

options.text: I do not know.
options.feedback: You do know. Explain who your friends are and where you will be.

step4.text: And what about your homework and chores? Have you finished your school work? Have you helped at home today?

options.text: I already finished my homework for today, and I helped sweep the floor. When I come back, I can also help with anything else you need.
options.feedback: Excellent. You show that you have met your responsibilities.

options.text: I will do homework later, maybe.
options.feedback: Show that you are responsible and that homework is important.

options.text: Homework is not important.
options.feedback: This is not acceptable. Your mother expects you to take school seriously.

step5.text: All right. Before 5 PM is okay. That gives you about one and a half hours. When the sun starts to go down, you must come home immediately. Do you understand?

options.text: Yes, Mama. I understand. I will come home before 5 PM and when it starts to get dark. I promise.
options.feedback: Very good. You confirm the rule and promise to obey.

options.text: Can I come home at 6 PM instead?
options.feedback: She already gave you a time. Do not push for a later hour.

options.text: Okay, 5 PM.
options.feedback: Add that you understand and accept the rule clearly.

step6.text: Good. Remember, do not play too hard and hurt yourself. You still have school tomorrow. Take a little money for water if you get thirsty, and be careful on the road.

options.text: Thank you, Mama! I will be careful on the road and I will come back before 5 PM. I will also be ready for school tomorrow. Thank you for letting me go.
options.feedback: Great ending. You show gratitude and responsibility.

options.text: Okay, I am going now.
options.feedback: Thank your mother and show appreciation for her permission.

options.text: Thank you, Mama. I will be home soon.
options.feedback: Good. You thank her and confirm your return.

scenarios.title: Explaining a Low Grade to Parents
scenarios.description: You got a low grade in English. You need to tell your parents and explain what happened.

start.text: How were your test results? Did you pass all your subjects?

options.text: I passed most subjects, but I got a low grade in English. I am sorry.
options.feedback: Honest start. You admit the low grade immediately.

options.text: Yes, all good.
options.feedback: You need to be honest about the low English grade.

options.text: The test was very hard.
options.feedback: Do not start with excuses. First say your real results.

step2.text: A low grade in English? How low? Show me the paper.

options.text: I got 11 out of 20. Here is my test paper. I made mistakes in verb tenses and I did not explain my answers clearly.
options.feedback: Good. You show the paper and explain the specific errors.

options.text: I do not have the paper.
options.feedback: You should show them the test so they can see what happened.

options.text: The teacher does not like me.
options.feedback: Do not blame the teacher. Look at your own work first.

step3.text: Eleven out of twenty is not good. Why did you do poorly? Did you study enough?

options.text: I did not study hard enough. I thought it would be easy, so I did not practice verb tenses and I did not read the instructions carefully.
options.feedback: Very honest. You accept responsibility for not studying enough.

options.text: I studied a little, but the test was too hard.
options.feedback: Be honest. You already said you did not study enough.

options.text: I studied the night before only.
options.feedback: This is part of the problem. You should also say how you will change this.

step4.text: This is not good, but we are glad you are honest. What will you do to improve your English grade? Do you have a plan?

options.text: Yes. I will study a bit every day, not just before the test. I will ask my teacher for extra exercises on verb tenses and I will do my homework more carefully.
options.feedback: Excellent plan. You have specific actions to improve.

options.text: I will study more next time.
options.feedback: Be specific. Say exactly what you will do differently.

options.text: I do not know. Maybe I will try.
options.feedback: You need a clear plan, not a vague answer.

step5.text: That is a good start. Do you want us to help you? We can check your homework or give you time and a quiet place to study. Maybe you can also study with a friend who is good at English.

options.text: Yes, that would help me a lot. If you can check my homework and let me study in a quiet place, I will focus better. I can also ask my friend who is good at English to study with me.
options.feedback: Good. You accept the support and agree to the suggestions.

options.text: No, I do not need help.
options.feedback: Accept support. It shows you are serious about improving.

options.text: I only want my friend to help.
options.feedback: Family support is important too. You can have both.

step6.text: All right. We will help you, but we also want to see a better result on your next test. Until then, you can only play outside after you finish homework and show it to us. Do you understand?

options.text: Yes, I understand. I will do my homework first, let you check it, and then I can play. I want to improve my English grade and make you proud.
options.feedback: Very good. You accept the conditions and show motivation.

options.text: But I want to play first.
options.feedback: You must show responsibility before play.

options.text: Yes, I understand. I am sorry for this low grade.
options.feedback: Good. You acknowledge the situation.

scenarios.title: Asking for Money for School Supplies
scenarios.description: You need to buy school supplies for next week. You ask your mother for money and explain what you need.

start.text: What do you want? You look serious.

options.text: Mama, the school gave me a list of things I need to buy. Can you give me money for these supplies, please?
options.feedback: Polite and direct. You state the purpose of the request.

options.text: I need money.
options.feedback: Say what you need the money for.

options.text: Can I have money for something?
options.feedback: Be clear and honest about the purpose.

step2.text: School supplies? What exactly do you need? Show me the list.

options.text: Yes, here is the list. I need two notebooks at 500 CFA each, five pens at 150 CFA each, one geometry set at 2000 CFA, and one book at 3500 CFA. The total is about 7000 CFA.
options.feedback: Very clear. You list the items and prices.

options.text: I need a lot of things.
options.feedback: Show her the list and give details.

options.text: I do not know the exact price.
options.feedback: Check the list and calculate. Your mother needs to know the total.

step3.text: Seven thousand CFA is a lot. Do you really need all of these things? Notebooks and pens, yes. But do you need a geometry set and such an expensive book?

options.text: Yes, Mama. The geometry set is for mathematics class – we use it to draw shapes. The book is our English textbook, and all students must have it. The school said they are required.
options.feedback: Good explanation. You justify why each item is necessary.

options.text: The school said I need them.
options.feedback: Explain what each item is used for in class.

options.text: I just want them.
options.feedback: They are not for fun. Explain that they are needed for lessons.

step4.text: I see. If they are required, you must have them. But our money is limited. Can you buy some things used or cheaper? Maybe buy the notebooks and pens now and the geometry set later?

options.text: I can look for cheaper notebooks and used pens, and I can ask if someone has an old geometry set to sell. But the English book is new for this year, so I need that one soon.
options.feedback: Very helpful. You offer ways to save money while explaining priorities.

options.text: No, I want everything new and expensive.
options.feedback: Try to help your mother save money where possible.

options.text: I do not know. You decide.
options.feedback: Show that you are thinking about costs and trying to help.

step5.text: That sounds reasonable. Here is 5000 CFA. Try to buy cheaper or used items so the money can cover everything you need now. If you still need more for the textbook, we will talk again. When do you need these things?

options.text: Thank you, Mama! I need them by next Friday. I will look for cheaper or used things and try to save money. If I cannot buy everything, I will tell you.
options.feedback: Excellent. You accept the money and the plan.

options.text: I need them today.
options.feedback: You said “next week” before. Give the correct deadline.

options.text: Thank you, Mama. I will buy what I can.
options.feedback: Also mention the date and that you will inform her if money is not enough.

step6.text: Good. After you buy them, come home and show me what you bought and how much you spent. If there is any change, bring it back to me. I want to see that you use the money well.

options.text: Yes, Mama. I will keep the receipts and bring you the supplies and any change. Thank you for trusting me with this money.
options.feedback: Perfect ending. You show responsibility and trustworthiness.

options.text: I might forget to bring the change.
options.feedback: This can break trust. Always bring back the remaining money.

options.text: Okay, I will show you the things when I come back.
options.feedback: Good. You agree to be accountable.

scenarios.title: Introducing a New Friend to Your Family
scenarios.description: You brought a new friend home to meet your family. Your parents are in the living room. You want to introduce your friend properly and help them feel comfortable.

start.text: Good afternoon! Who is this young person with you?

options.text: Good afternoon, Mama. This is my friend from school. Her name is Grace. I want you to meet her.
This is my friend.
options.feedback: Say your friend's name and where you know her from.

options.text: She is my friend.
options.feedback: Use a polite introduction, for example, 'This is my friend Grace from school.'

step2.text: Welcome, Grace! It is nice to meet you. Where are you from? Do you go to the same school as my child?

options.text: Yes, Mama. Grace is in my class. We study together. She is from Douala, but her family moved here last year.
Yes, she is my friend from school.
options.feedback: Add a little more detail – what class, where she is from.

options.text: I do not know much about her.
options.feedback: You brought her home, so you should know some basic things.

step3.text: That is nice. Grace, you are welcome here. Feel at home.

options.text: Grace, you can greet my parents. (Grace): Good afternoon, Mama. Good afternoon, Papa. Thank you for welcoming me.
Stay silent and let Grace speak alone.
options.feedback: Help your friend know what to say. You can guide her to greet your parents.

options.text: Grace is shy. She does not like to talk.
options.feedback: Encourage your friend politely instead of speaking for her in a negative way.

step4.text: Good afternoon. Welcome to our home, Grace. How are your studies going?

options.text: Grace is doing well in school. She is very good at mathematics. We study together in the library.
She is okay.
options.feedback: Give a more complete answer. Say something positive about your friend.

options.text: Grace, answer my father.
options.feedback: You can let Grace answer, but also support her with a short introduction.

step5.text: That is good. Mathematics is important. What are your plans after school, Grace? Do you want to go to university?

options.text: Grace wants to study nursing at university. She wants to help people. She is a very kind person.
I do not know her plans very well.
options.feedback: As close friends, you probably know her dreams. Share what you know briefly.

options.text: Ask Grace yourself.
options.feedback: You can let Grace speak, but also show that you know and support her goals.

step6.text: Nursing is a wonderful job! We need good nurses. Before you go to your room, I want you both to know our rules: when you are in the house, you must keep the noise low and you cannot stay too late. What time do you plan to finish your work or play?

options.text: We will sit in my room and do homework for about one hour. After that, we may talk a little, but Grace will go home before 6 PM.
We do not know. Maybe very late.
options.feedback: Give a clear and reasonable time so your parents feel comfortable.

options.text: We will not be noisy.
options.feedback: Also say what time your friend will leave.

step7.text: That is fine. Come, Grace, would you like to sit down? Can I bring you some water or juice? And you, do you want something to eat?

options.text: Thank you, Mama. Grace would like some water, please. I would also like a little snack if you have it.
No, we are fine.
options.feedback: Ask your friend first. Do not refuse for her without checking.

options.text: Yes, please. We are hungry. Anything you have is fine.

scenarios.title: Explaining Why You Are Late Coming Home
scenarios.description: You told your mother you would be home at 4 PM, but you did not arrive until 5:30 PM. Your mother is worried and a little upset. You need to explain what happened and apologize.

start.text: Where have you been? You said you would be home at 4 PM! It is now 5:30 PM! I was very worried!

options.text: Mama, I am very sorry. I know I was late. Something happened. Can I explain what happened?
I was at my friend's house.
options.feedback: First apologize and then explain.

options.text: I am sorry.
options.feedback: Say sorry and also ask to explain the situation.

step2.text: Yes, explain. Why were you so late? What happened?

options.text: My teacher gave me extra homework at the last minute. It took longer than I expected. Then my friend and I needed to study together, so I stayed at her house longer. I lost track of time.
I forgot about the time.
options.feedback: This is not enough. Say what you were doing when you forgot.

options.text: We were just talking.
options.feedback: That shows you did not manage your time well. Explain more and show responsibility.

step3.text: You lost track of time? That is not acceptable. Why did you not call me or send a message? You have a phone.

options.text: You are right, Mama. I should have called you. My phone battery was low, but I still could have borrowed my friend's phone. I did not think clearly. I am really sorry.
I did not feel like calling.
options.feedback: This shows no respect. You must show that you understand her worry.

options.text: I thought you would not be worried.
options.feedback: Of course she worries. She is your mother. Acknowledge her feelings.

step4.text: I am your mother. When you are late and you do not call, I think something bad may have happened. Next time, I might have to go out and look for you.

options.text: I understand, Mama. I did not think about how you felt. I am very sorry for making you worry. Next time I will always call if I am going to be late.
But nothing bad happened this time.
options.feedback: That is not the point. The problem is that she did not know you were safe.

options.text: You do not need to worry so much.
options.feedback: This is not respectful. Accept that she worries because she loves you.

step5.text: Good. So from now on: if you are going to be more than 15 minutes late, you must call or send a message. If you do not, I will not let you go out with friends next time. Do you accept this rule?

options.text: Yes, Mama. I accept this rule. If I am more than 15 minutes late, I will call or send a message. I do not want to make you worry again.
Fifteen minutes is too short. Make it one hour.
options.feedback: Do not negotiate now. Show that you accept and understand.

options.text: I will try.
options.feedback: Say clearly that you will do it, not only 'try'.

step6.text: All right. I believe you this time. But if it happens again, there will be consequences. Now go wash your hands and come for dinner.

options.text: Thank you, Mama. I love you and I am grateful that you care about me. I will be more responsible from now on.
Okay, I am hungry.
options.feedback: Say thank you and show appreciation before you talk about food.

options.text: Okay, I will come.

scenarios.title: Asking for Directions to the Hospital
scenarios.description: You need to go to the hospital but you are not sure how to get there. You are walking down the street and you see an older man. You stop to ask him for directions.

start.text: Good morning! Can I help you with something?

options.text: Good morning, sir. I am looking for the hospital. Can you tell me how to get there, please?
Where is the hospital?
options.feedback: Be polite. Start with a greeting and 'please'.

options.text: I am lost.
options.feedback: Say where you want to go, not only that you are lost.

step2.text: The hospital? Yes, it is not far. You go straight down this road for about five minutes. Then you turn right at the big market. You cannot miss it – it is a big white building next to the market.

options.text: Thank you, sir. So I go straight for five minutes, then turn right at the market. Is the hospital on the right side or the left side of the market?
Okay, thank you.
options.feedback: Repeat the directions to check you understood and ask one small question.

options.text: Can I take a taxi instead?
options.feedback: First show you understood the walking directions. You can ask about a taxi later.

step3.text: The hospital is on the left side as you face the market. You will see a big sign that says 'Hospital' on the gate. There is also a pharmacy right in front of it.

options.text: So, straight for five minutes, then right at the big market, and the hospital is on the left side with a sign and a pharmacy nearby. If I reach the petrol station, did I go too far?
Left side, okay.
options.feedback: Repeat the full directions to be sure and ask if there is a point where you know you went too far.

options.text: I still do not understand.
options.feedback: The directions are clear. Repeat them to help yourself remember.

step4.text: Yes, if you see the petrol station, you went too far. Turn back towards the market. Also, be careful when you cross the road near the market – there are many cars and motorbikes.

options.text: Thank you for the warning, sir. I will be careful when I cross the road near the market. I really appreciate your help.
I am not afraid of the road.
options.feedback: The man is just caring. Say thank you and show respect for his advice.

options.text: I know how to cross.
options.feedback: You can still say thank you. He is trying to help you.

step5.text: You are welcome. The hospital has good doctors. Go with God, my child. I hope you or the person you are visiting will be fine.

options.text: Thank you, sir. I am visiting a friend there. Your directions help a lot. Have a good day!
Thank you.
options.feedback: It is better to add a short, warm message back, like 'Have a good day.'

options.text: I will find it somehow.
options.feedback: This sounds ungrateful. Show appreciation instead.

scenarios.title: Finding the Way to a Government Office
scenarios.description: You need to go to the government office to get a document. You are at the main traffic circle in your town. You see a woman selling things at a kiosk. You ask her for directions to the office.

start.text: Good afternoon! Do you need something?

options.text: Good afternoon. Excuse me, can you help me, please? I am looking for the government office. Do you know where it is?
I need the government office.
options.feedback: Add a greeting and 'please' to be polite.

options.text: Do you work for the government?
options.feedback: You do not need to know that. Just ask for directions.

step2.text: The government office? Yes, I know where it is. It is a little far from here, but you can reach it. Go down that road over there – past the bank and the school. When you reach the clinic, turn left. The government office is about one block after the clinic.

options.text: Thank you. So I go past the bank and the school, then turn left at the clinic, and the office is one block after. Is it on the right or on the left side of the road?
That sounds far. Can I take a taxi?
options.feedback: First show you understood the directions. Then you can ask about transport.

options.text: I do not understand. Can you come with me?
options.feedback: She is working. Do not ask her to leave her kiosk.

step3.text: The office is on the right side of the road. You will see a big gate with the national flag and a sign that says 'Sub-divisional Office'. There is a small park just before it.

options.text: Okay, I understand: right side of the road, big gate, flag, and a sign. Is the office open every day, or only on weekdays?
I will just look for a big gate.
options.feedback: Repeat more of the details she gave you to be sure you remember.

options.text: I will see the flag, so that is enough.
options.feedback: Use all the information – gate, sign, flag, and park – to be sure.

step4.text: It is open from Monday to Friday, 8 AM to 4 PM. On Saturday they are sometimes open in the morning, but it is not sure. If you want, you can take a taxi from here. Just tell the driver 'government office near the clinic'.

options.text: Thank you very much. What time is it now? I want to be sure I arrive before they close.
I will go on Saturday.
options.feedback: Saturday is not sure. Better to go on a weekday if you can.

options.text: I will just go and see.
options.feedback: You should check the time now so you can plan.

step5.text: It is about 2:15 PM. If you walk, it may take 30 minutes. If you take a taxi, it will take maybe 10 minutes.

options.text: That helps. I think I will take a taxi so I arrive early. Thank you for telling me the time and the directions. You have helped me a lot.
I will walk. I do not care about the time.
options.feedback: You should care. The office closes at 4 PM. Say you will watch the time.

options.text: I am not sure what to do.
options.feedback: Choose one: walk or taxi, but in both cases, aim to arrive early.

step6.text: You are welcome. Go straight, follow what I said, and you will find it. May your document be ready quickly!

options.text: Thank you again. I hope so too. Have a good afternoon and good business!
Bye.
options.feedback: Add a short thank you and good wish.

options.text: Okay, I am going.
options.feedback: It is polite to thank her clearly for her help.

scenarios.title: Asking About a Bus Route
scenarios.description: You want to go to the next town using the bus. You see a man standing at the bus station. He looks like he knows about the buses. You ask him about the route and schedule.

start.text: Hello! Are you looking for a bus?

options.text: Yes, hello. I want to go to Buea. Do you know which bus goes there?
Yes.
options.feedback: Say where you want to go.

options.text: I am lost.
options.feedback: You are at a bus station – tell him your destination.

step2.text: Buea? Yes, the express bus goes to Buea. It leaves every two hours. The next bus leaves at 3 PM.

options.text: Thank you. What time is it now? And how long does it take to go to Buea? And how much is the fare?
Okay, I will take the 3 PM bus.
options.feedback: Ask about the price and travel time first so you can plan.

options.text: Is it safe?
options.feedback: The express bus is the normal way to go. First ask about time and fare.

step3.text: It is 2 PM now. The bus takes about two hours to get to Buea. And the fare is 3500 CFA.

options.text: So the bus leaves at 3 PM, takes about two hours, and costs 3500 CFA. That means I will arrive around 5 PM. Do I need to buy my ticket now, or can I pay on the bus?
That is expensive!
options.feedback: 3500 CFA is normal for an express bus. Do not complain; just decide if you can pay or not.

options.text: I do not have enough money.
options.feedback: If you cannot pay, you cannot travel now. But still ask about the ticket process to know for next time.

step4.text: You should buy your ticket before you get on. The ticket office is that small building there. They will give you a seat number. If you wait until the last minute, the bus might be full.

options.text: Thank you. I will buy the ticket now so I get a seat. Do they put luggage under the bus, or do I keep my bag with me?
I will just jump on the bus when it comes.
options.feedback: That is risky. It may be full and you may not be allowed without a ticket.

options.text: I will wait until 3 PM, then buy the ticket.
options.feedback: If you wait, tickets might be finished. Buy early.

step5.text: Big bags go under the bus in the luggage compartment. Small bags you can keep with you. Keep your important things like money and phone in your small bag.

options.text: That is helpful. I have one small bag, so I will keep it with me. Thank you for the advice. Is there anything else I should know?
I will put everything under the bus.
options.feedback: It is safer to keep your money and phone with you.

options.text: I do not care about my things.
options.feedback: You should care. Keep your important documents and money safe.

step6.text: Just be at the bus about 10 or 15 minutes before 3 PM so you can find your seat calmly. Then sit and keep your ticket with you. Have a safe trip.

options.text: Thank you very much for all your help. I will buy my ticket now and be at the bus early. Have a good day!
Okay.
options.feedback: Add a clear thank you. He gave you a lot of information.

options.text: I hope the bus is not late.
options.feedback: You can say that, but also thank him properly.

scenarios.title: Finding a Specific Shop in Town
scenarios.description: You are walking in town and you need to find a phone repair shop. You have heard there is one near the main road, but you do not know exactly where. You ask a young woman who is walking past you.

start.text: Good afternoon! Are you looking for something?

options.text: Good afternoon. Yes, I am looking for a phone repair shop. Do you know where one is near here?
I am lost.
options.feedback: Say what you are looking for, for example, 'I am lost. I am looking for a phone repair shop.'

options.text: Do you work here?
options.feedback: You do not need to know that. Just ask about the shop you need.

step2.text: A phone repair shop? There are a few in town. Do you want the small one in the market, or the bigger one near the main road?

options.text: I am looking for the one near the main road. I heard they repair smartphones and sell phone covers too.
Any phone shop is fine.
options.feedback: Say clearly which area you want – near the main road or in the market – so she can give exact directions.

options.text: I do not know. Just one where they repair phones.
options.feedback: Choose one area – market or main road – to help her guide you.

step3.text: The big shop near the main road, yes, I know it. It is called 'Quick Fix Phones'. They repair phones and also sell phone credit and chargers. It is close to the supermarket on Main Road.

options.text: Great! Can you tell me how to get to the supermarket on Main Road from here? Is it far?
Thank you, I will find it.
options.feedback: Ask for clear directions from where you are now to the supermarket.

options.text: Are you sure it is called 'Quick Fix Phones'?
options.feedback: The name is not very important. Focus on how to get there.

step4.text: The supermarket is not far, about ten minutes' walk. You see that big junction ahead? Go straight to the junction, then turn left. Walk straight until you see a big orange building on your right – that is the supermarket.

options.text: Thank you. So I walk to the junction, turn left, and go straight until I see the orange supermarket on my right. Where exactly is the phone shop from there?
Left at the junction, orange building, okay.
options.feedback: Repeat the directions fully and ask about the exact position of the phone shop.

options.text: I will just ask someone else when I reach the junction.
options.feedback: You already have someone helping you. Get the full directions now.

step5.text: When you reach the supermarket, face the building. The phone repair shop is just next to it on the left side, with a sign that says 'Quick Fix Phones'. They open from 8 AM to 6 PM, Monday to Saturday.

options.text: So it is next to the supermarket on the left, with a sign 'Quick Fix Phones', open until 6 PM. Do they fix cracked screens, or only small problems?
Next to the supermarket, okay.
options.feedback: Repeat more details to help you remember – left side, sign, opening time.

options.text: Do they sell food too?
options.feedback: It is a phone repair shop, not a food shop. Ask about their phone services instead.

step6.text: Yes, they fix cracked screens, change batteries, and repair chargers. They are usually quick and not too expensive. I hope they can fix your phone.

options.text: Thank you so much! You are very kind. I will go there now – junction, left, orange supermarket, then 'Quick Fix Phones' on the left. Have a good day!
Thanks.
options.feedback: Add a sentence to show you understood the directions and appreciate her help.

options.text: Goodbye.
options.feedback: Say goodbye and also thank her for the detailed help.

scenarios.title: Asking a Stranger for Directions When You Are Lost
scenarios.description: You are lost in a part of town you do not know. You have been walking for twenty minutes and you are going the wrong way. You see an old woman sitting on a bench. You ask her for help.

start.text: Hello, young person. You look confused. What is the problem?

options.text: Good afternoon, Ma. I am lost. I am looking for the market, but I cannot find it. Can you help me, please?
I am lost.
options.feedback: Add where you want to go, for example, 'I am lost. I am looking for the main market.'

options.text: What is this place?
options.feedback: The place is not important. Say where you want to go.

step2.text: Lost? Come, sit here a moment. You look tired. The market is not far from here. But which market are you looking for? There are many markets in town.

options.text: Thank you, Ma. I am looking for the main market – the big one where people sell vegetables and fish.
The market near my house.
options.feedback: She does not know your house. Say the name or describe the market.

options.text: Any market is fine.
options.feedback: Be specific so she can guide you to the correct place.

step3.text: The big vegetable market! Yes, I know it. Listen carefully. You went too far. You must go back the way you came. Turn around here and walk back down this road. After about five minutes, you will see a church on your right. Turn left after the church. The market is two blocks down.

options.text: Thank you, Ma. So I go back down this road, then turn left after the church, and the market is two blocks away. Can you repeat once more so I am sure?
That is too complicated. I am still confused.
options.feedback: Ask her to repeat slowly instead of saying it is complicated.

options.text: Okay, thank you!
options.feedback: Ask her to repeat once more. It is easy to forget the steps when you are tired.

step4.text: All right, listen again. Turn around, walk back for five minutes. Watch for a white church with a cross on the roof on your right. After that church, turn left. Then walk two blocks – you will smell the fish and hear people shouting prices. That is the market.

options.text: Now I understand, Ma. Turn around, walk back, see the white church, turn left, then two blocks to the busy place with fish and vegetables. If I see a petrol station, did I go too far?
I think I know now.
options.feedback: Repeat the directions in your own words to check your understanding.

options.text: I will just follow other people.
options.feedback: Better to follow the clear directions she gave.

step5.text: If you see the petrol station, yes, you went too far. Turn back towards the church. But do not worry – many people are going to the market. If you are not sure, ask again. It is a safe area.

options.text: Thank you so much, Ma. You are very kind. I will follow your directions exactly. I feel less worried now.
I hope I will not get lost again.
options.feedback: Also thank her warmly. She took time to help you.

options.text: Are you sure it is safe?
options.feedback: She already said it is safe. Trust her and thank her.

step6.text: You are welcome, my child. Go carefully, and drink water when you get home – you look tired.

options.text: Thank you, Ma. You are like my grandmother! Have a good afternoon.
Okay, bye.
options.feedback: Add a thank you or kind word – she helped you kindly.

options.text: I will go now.
options.feedback: Say thank you before you leave.

scenarios.title: Asking for a Job at a Shop
scenarios.description: You see a sign on a shop window that says 'Workers Wanted.' You are looking for a job, so you go inside and ask the manager about the position.

start.text: Good morning! Welcome to our shop. Can I help you?

options.text: Good morning, sir. I saw your sign that says 'Workers Wanted.' Are you still looking for workers?
I want a job.
options.feedback: Be polite and mention the sign you saw.

options.text: Are you the manager?
options.feedback: You can assume he works here. Go directly to asking about the job.

step2.text: Yes, we are still hiring. Are you interested in working here? How old are you? Have you worked before?

options.text: Yes, I am interested. I am eighteen years old. I have not worked in a shop before, but I helped my father in his small business. I am a hard worker and I learn quickly.
Yes, I want to work here.
options.feedback: Answer all his questions – age and experience.

options.text: I just finished school.
options.feedback: Also say your age and experience, and that you are interested in the job.

step3.text: Good. Can you read and write? Can you use a calculator? And how many hours can you work per day?

options.text: Yes, sir, I can read and write well. I finished secondary school and I can use a calculator. I can work full time – eight hours per day, from morning to evening.
Yes, I can work many hours.
options.feedback: Be specific: how many hours and what time, for example, 8 AM to 5 PM.

options.text: I can only work when I want.
options.feedback: Jobs have fixed hours. Say clearly when you are available.

step4.text: All right. The job is to help customers, arrange the shelves, clean the shop, and sometimes count money at the end of the day. You would work from 8 AM to 5 PM, with one hour for lunch. The pay is 25000 CFA per month. Do you understand?

options.text: Yes, sir. I understand: work from 8 AM to 5 PM, one hour lunch, help customers, arrange shelves, clean, and sometimes count money. The pay is 25000 CFA per month. That is clear.
25000 CFA is not enough.
options.feedback: Do not complain at the start. First show you understand the job.

options.text: What days will I work?
options.feedback: Good question, but first confirm you understood what he already explained.

step5.text: You will work from Monday to Saturday. Sunday is your day off. We also expect you to be on time every day and to be polite with customers.

options.text: Monday to Saturday, Sunday off. I understand. I will be on time and polite with customers. I like working with people. When could I start, if you choose me?
Six days is too much.
options.feedback: Many shop jobs are six days. If you really cannot, explain your situation politely.

options.text: Can I choose which days I work?
options.feedback: The manager already said Monday to Saturday. You cannot choose days as you like.

step6.text: You seem serious and polite. If you want the job, you can start tomorrow at 8 AM. Wear clean clothes; we will give you a uniform. Bring a copy of your ID card.

options.text: Yes, sir, I would like the job. Thank you very much for trusting me. I will bring my ID copy and come tomorrow at 8 AM. I will work hard.
Okay, I will come.
options.feedback: Add thanks and repeat the time to show you listened.

options.text: Can I start next week?
options.feedback: He offered tomorrow. If you have a real problem, explain it politely; do not just delay without reason.

scenarios.title: Reporting a Problem to Your Supervisor
scenarios.description: You have been working at a restaurant for three weeks. You noticed that some customers are complaining that the food comes very slowly. You think there is a problem in the kitchen. You want to report this to your supervisor.

start.text: Good afternoon. Is everything okay? You look like you want to talk about something.

options.text: Good afternoon, sir. Yes, I want to tell you about something I noticed. Do you have a moment to talk?
There is a problem.
options.feedback: Be polite and ask if he has a moment first.

options.text: I have a complaint.
options.feedback: It is better to say 'something I noticed' than 'complaint'.

step2.text: Yes, I have time. What is it? Tell me what you noticed.

options.text: Sir, I have been here for three weeks, and I noticed that many customers are complaining about slow service. The food takes a very long time to come to the table. I think there might be a problem in the kitchen.
Customers say the food is slow.
options.feedback: Add how long you have noticed this and how often it happens.

options.text: The kitchen is too slow.
options.feedback: This sounds like blame. Describe what customers say instead.

step3.text: I see. Slow service. Can you give me some examples? When did you first notice this, and how many customers complained?

options.text: I first noticed it about one week ago. At first, only one or two customers complained, but this week about five or six customers said something. Some waited more than forty minutes for their food, especially in the evening.
Many customers complained yesterday.
options.feedback: Try to give numbers and time periods, not just 'many'.

options.text: Every day the food is slow.
options.feedback: If you say 'every day', be ready to give examples. Be accurate.

step4.text: Forty minutes is too long. Thank you for telling me. Do you have any idea what might be causing the delay?

options.text: I am not sure, sir. I noticed that when we have many orders, the kitchen looks very busy, and sometimes only two people are working there. Maybe there are not enough staff, or maybe some equipment is slow. But I do not go inside the kitchen, so I cannot see everything.
The cooks are lazy.
options.feedback: Do not attack people. Talk about what you see, not about their character.

options.text: They do not know how to work fast.
options.feedback: You do not know that. Stay neutral and factual.

step5.text: I understand. It might be a staffing or equipment problem. What do you think we can do to help the situation from your side in the dining area?

options.text: Maybe we can tell customers honestly if the food will take longer, and offer them water while they wait. We can also write down orders clearly so the kitchen does not lose time reading them.
It is not my problem. It is the kitchen's problem.
options.feedback: You are part of a team. Show that you care about the customers and the restaurant.

options.text: We cannot do anything.
options.feedback: Even small actions, like informing customers, can help.

step6.text: Those are good ideas. I will talk to the kitchen staff and the owner about adding one more person during busy hours. In the meantime, please do what you suggested – inform customers if there is a delay and offer water.

options.text: Thank you, sir. I will do that. I want the customers to be happy, and I am glad you are taking this seriously.
Okay.
options.feedback: Add that you will follow his instructions and that you care about customer satisfaction.

options.text: I hope the kitchen changes.
options.feedback: Also thank him and say what you will do personally.

scenarios.title: Asking for Permission to Leave Work Early
scenarios.description: You work in an office. Your mother called you and told you that your younger brother is sick and she needs you to come home to help her. You need to ask your supervisor if you can leave work two hours early.

start.text: Good afternoon. How is your work today?

options.text: Good afternoon, sir. My work is going well, but I need to ask you something important. Is now a good time?
I need to leave early.
options.feedback: First ask if it is a good time to talk, then explain.

options.text: I have a problem.
options.feedback: Say you have a question and ask if he has a moment.

step2.text: Yes, I have a moment. What do you want to ask?

options.text: My mother called me just now. My younger brother is sick and she needs help at home. I would like to ask if I can leave work two hours early today – at 3 PM instead of 5 PM.
I want to go home early.
options.feedback: Explain the reason clearly – your brother is sick and your mother needs help.

options.text: There is a family problem.
options.feedback: Say what kind of family problem, at least in general terms.

step3.text: I am sorry to hear your brother is sick. Is it serious? Has he seen a doctor already, or are you going to take him?

options.text: My mother says it is not very serious, but he has fever and she is worried. She wants me to help take him to the clinic and look after him. We live close by, so if I leave at 3 PM, I can reach home quickly.
I do not know. She just said he is sick.
options.feedback: Try to know a little more so you can answer questions clearly.

options.text: Yes, it is very serious.
options.feedback: Do not exaggerate if it is not life-threatening. Be honest.

step4.text: I understand. Family is important. You have tasks to finish today. Can you complete the most urgent work before 3 PM, and can you come in a bit earlier tomorrow to catch up?

options.text: Yes, sir. I can finish the urgent tasks before 3 PM, and I will come in early tomorrow to catch up on the rest. I do not want my work here to suffer.
I will do it another day.
options.feedback: He asked if you can finish today and come early tomorrow. Answer that question directly.

options.text: I cannot come early tomorrow.
options.feedback: If there is a real reason, explain it. If not, try to accept his condition.

step5.text: All right. You may leave at 3 PM today. Please send me a short email before you go, listing what you finished and what is still pending, so I know the situation.

options.text: Thank you very much, sir. I will send you an email before 3 PM with the tasks I finished and the ones I still need to do. I really appreciate your understanding.
Okay, I will just go at 3 PM.
options.feedback: Confirm that you will send the email and say thank you.

options.text: Do I really need to send an email?
options.feedback: He asked you to. Accept the instruction politely.

step6.text: Good. Take care of your brother and help your mother. Family emergencies happen. See you tomorrow morning.

options.text: Thank you again, sir. I will go at 3 PM, after finishing my urgent work and sending you the email. I will also tell my mother that you were understanding. See you tomorrow morning.
Goodbye.
options.feedback: Add thanks and confirm what you will do before you leave.

options.text: Thank you, sir.

scenarios.title: Explaining Why You Cannot Come to Work
scenarios.description: You wake up feeling very sick with a high fever. You cannot go to work. You need to call your boss to explain and say you will go to the hospital.

start.text: Hello, this is Mr. Talla. Why are you calling me so early?

options.text: Good morning, Mr. Talla. I am very sorry to call you early, but I am not feeling well today. I have a high fever and I cannot come to work.
I am sick.
options.feedback: Be more polite and explain clearly. Say 'Good morning' and apologize for the early call.

options.text: I am not coming.
options.feedback: That is rude. Explain why you cannot come and be polite.

step2.text: Oh, I see. You were fine yesterday. What is wrong exactly? Is it malaria?

options.text: I think so, sir. I have a headache, fever, and I feel very weak. I am going to the hospital now to do a test.
I don't know.
options.feedback: Describe your symptoms so he understands it is serious.

options.text: Maybe.
options.feedback: Give more details about how you feel.

step3.text: Okay. Health is important. But we have a lot of work today. When do you think you can come back?

options.text: I hope to be back tomorrow if the doctor says it is okay. I will call you later to tell you what the doctor says.
I will come when I am better.
options.feedback: Give an estimated time, like 'tomorrow', to show you are responsible.

options.text: Maybe next week.
options.feedback: That is too long without a doctor's note. Say you will call after seeing the doctor.

step4.text: All right. Go to the hospital. Call me after you see the doctor. Do not forget to bring a medical certificate when you return.

options.text: Yes, sir. I will get the medical certificate and call you later. Thank you for understanding.
Okay.
options.feedback: Confirm about the certificate and thank him for letting you stay home.

options.text: Bye.
options.feedback: Be polite. Say thank you and goodbye properly.

scenarios.title: Asking for a Loan from a Friend
scenarios.description: You have an urgent problem and need money. You want to ask your close friend to lend you 10,000 CFA. You promise to pay it back next week.

start.text: Hey! How are you doing? Long time no see.

options.text: I am fine, thanks. Listen, I have a small problem and I need to ask you for a favor. Can we talk?
Give me money.
options.feedback: That is too direct and rude. Ask nicely if you can talk about a problem.

options.text: I have a problem.
options.feedback: Ask if you can talk about it first.

step2.text: Sure, what is going on? You sound serious.

options.text: I have an urgent bill to pay today and I am short of cash. Could you please lend me 10,000 CFA? I will pay you back next week when I get my salary.
I need 10,000 CFA.
options.feedback: Explain why and when you will pay back. Be polite.

options.text: Can you help me?
options.feedback: Be specific about what you need and how much.

step3.text: 10,000 CFA? That is a bit tight for me too right now. Are you sure you can pay me back next week?

options.text: Yes, I promise. I get paid on Monday, so I will bring the money to you on Monday evening. I really appreciate your help.
Trust me.
options.feedback: Give a specific day when you will pay back to reassure him.

options.text: Maybe.
options.feedback: You must be sure if you are borrowing money.

step4.text: Okay, because we are friends, I will do it. But please do not forget on Monday.

options.text: Thank you so much! You are a true friend. I will not forget. Monday evening, I promise.
Thanks.
options.feedback: Reassure him again that you will not forget.

options.text: Okay.
options.feedback: Show more appreciation. He is doing you a big favor.

scenarios.title: Refusing a Request for Money
scenarios.description: An acquaintance asks you to lend them money. You do not have enough money to spare, or you do not want to lend it. You need to refuse politely but firmly.

start.text: Hello! My friend, I am in a difficult situation. Can you lend me 5,000 CFA? I will pay you back soon.

options.text: Hello. I am sorry to hear you have a problem, but I cannot lend you money right now. I have many expenses myself.
No, I don't have money.
options.feedback: That is a bit blunt. Be polite but firm.

options.text: Ask someone else.
options.feedback: Explain why you cannot help before suggesting others.

step2.text: Oh, come on. Just 5,000 CFA. I know you have a job. Please, I really need it.

options.text: I understand, but I really cannot help you this time. My budget is very tight this month. I hope you find another solution.
I said no.
options.feedback: Stay calm and polite. Repeat your refusal firmly.

options.text: Maybe later.
options.feedback: If you mean no, say no clearly. Do not give false hope.

step3.text: You are stingy! But okay, if you cannot, you cannot.

options.text: I am sorry you feel that way, but I have to manage my own money. Good luck.
Don't call me stingy.
options.feedback: Do not argue. Just end the conversation politely.

options.text: Okay, bye.
options.feedback: Close the conversation politely.

scenarios.title: Apologizing for Breaking Something
scenarios.description: You borrowed a book from a friend and you accidentally spilled coffee on it. You need to apologize and offer to replace it.

start.text: Hi! Did you finish reading my book? Can I have it back?

options.text: Hi. I am so sorry, but I have some bad news. I accidentally spilled coffee on your book.
Here is your book.
options.feedback: You must tell him about the damage before giving it back.

options.text: I lost it.
options.feedback: Tell the truth about what happened.

step2.text: What? You spilled coffee on it? Is it ruined?

options.text: Yes, some pages are stained. I feel terrible about it because I know you like that book. I want to buy you a new copy.
It is just a little coffee.
options.feedback: Do not minimize the problem. It is his property.

options.text: Sorry.
options.feedback: Offer a solution, like replacing the book.

step3.text: It was a gift from my sister. I am really upset.

options.text: I understand completely. I am very sorry. I will go to the bookstore today and buy the exact same edition for you. Please forgive me.
I will buy another one.
options.feedback: Acknowledge his feelings and apologize sincerely.

options.text: Don't be angry.
options.feedback: He has a right to be upset. Apologize again.

step4.text: Okay. If you replace it with a new one, I will forgive you. But please be more careful next time.

options.text: Thank you. I promise I will be more careful. I will bring the new book to you tomorrow.
Okay.
options.feedback: Reiterate your promise and say when you will bring the book.

options.text: It happens.
options.feedback: Take responsibility and promise to be careful.

scenarios.title: Complaining About Noise to a Neighbor
scenarios.description: Your neighbor plays loud music late at night. You cannot sleep. You go to their door to ask them to turn it down.

start.text: (Knock on door) Who is it? What do you want?

options.text: Good evening. I am your neighbor. I am sorry to disturb you, but your music is very loud and I cannot sleep.
Stop the noise!
options.feedback: Be polite first. Introduce yourself.

options.text: Open the door!
options.feedback: Introduce yourself and explain why you are there.

step2.text: Oh, is it too loud? I didn't realize. It's my birthday.

options.text: Happy birthday! I understand you are celebrating, but it is 11 PM and I have to work tomorrow. Could you please lower the volume a little?
I don't care. Turn it off.
options.feedback: Be reasonable. Ask to lower it, not necessarily turn it off completely.

options.text: It is too loud.
options.feedback: Acknowledge the birthday but explain your need to sleep.

step3.text: Okay, okay. I don't want trouble. I will turn it down.

options.text: Thank you very much. I appreciate it. Enjoy your party, but just a bit quieter, please. Goodnight.
Good.
options.feedback: Be polite to maintain good relations with your neighbor.

options.text: If you don't, I will call the police.
options.feedback: Don't threaten if he already agreed to turn it down.

scenarios.title: Asking for Help with a Heavy Load
scenarios.description: You are carrying a heavy box of books up the stairs. It is too heavy for you. You see a young man walking down. You ask him for help.

start.text: Hello. Be careful with that box. It looks heavy.

options.text: Hello. Yes, it is very heavy. Could you please help me carry it up the stairs?
Help me.
options.feedback: Be polite. Ask 'Could you please help me?'

options.text: It is heavy.
options.feedback: Ask for help directly, do not just complain.

step2.text: Sure, I can help you. Where are you taking it?

options.text: Thank you so much. I am taking it to the office on the second floor. It is the first door on the right.
Upstairs.
options.feedback: Be more specific. Tell him exactly where to go.

options.text: Just here.
options.feedback: Tell him exactly where you want to put it.

step3.text: Okay, let's go. Phew, it is heavy indeed! What is inside? Stones?

options.text: (Laughs) No, just books! But there are many of them. Thank you for your strength.
Books.
options.feedback: Be friendly. Answer his joke with a smile.

options.text: It is none of your business.
options.feedback: He is helping you. Be nice and polite.

step4.text: Here we are. Second floor. Where should I put it?

options.text: Please put it on that table near the window. That would be perfect.
There.
options.feedback: Point and explain clearly where you want it.

options.text: On the floor.
options.feedback: Be polite. Say 'Please put it on the floor.'

step5.text: Done. Do you need anything else?

options.text: No, that is all. You really saved me. I could not have done it alone. Thank you very much!
No.
options.feedback: Thank him warmly for his help.

options.text: You can go.
options.feedback: That is rude. Say thank you and goodbye properly.

scenarios.title: Negotiating a Price for a Taxi Ride
scenarios.description: You stop a taxi to go to the airport. The driver asks for a price that is too high. You want to negotiate a lower price.

start.text: Taxi! Where to?

options.text: Good morning. I am going to the airport. How much is it?
Airport.
options.feedback: Ask for the price first so you can negotiate.

options.text: Take me to the airport.
options.feedback: Agree on the price before you get in.

step2.text: The airport? That is far. It will be 5,000 CFA.

options.text: 5,000 CFA? That is too expensive. I usually pay 3,000 CFA for this trip.
Okay, let's go.
options.feedback: You wanted to negotiate. Try to ask for a lower price.

options.text: You are a thief!
options.feedback: Be polite even if the price is high. Just say it is too expensive.

step3.text: Fuel is expensive these days, my friend. 3,000 is too low. Give me 4,500.

options.text: I understand, but 4,500 is still too much for me. I can give you 3,500 CFA. That is a fair price.

options.feedback: Try to compromise a little to reach an agreement.

options.text: I will find another taxi.
options.feedback: You can try one more offer first before giving up.

step4.text: 3,500? Hmmm. Make it 4,000 and we go right now.

options.text: Okay, 4,000 CFA is fine. But please drive carefully and use the highway to be fast.

options.feedback: 4,000 is a good compromise. Accept it to save time.

options.text: Okay.
options.feedback: Confirm the price clearly.

step5.text: Agreed. 4,000 CFA. Get in.

options.text: Thank you. Here is my bag. Let's go.
Wait.
options.feedback: Get in if you agreed on the price.

options.text: Don't cheat me.
options.feedback: You already agreed on the price. Be polite now.

scenarios.title: Explaining a Mistake to a Customer
scenarios.description: You work in a shop. A customer ordered a blue shirt, but you accidentally sent him a red one. He comes to the shop to complain. You need to apologize and fix the mistake.

start.text: Excuse me! I ordered a blue shirt, but look what I got! A red shirt! What is this?

options.text: Good morning, sir. I am very sorry for the mistake. Please let me check your order.
It is not my fault.
options.feedback: Take responsibility on behalf of the shop. Apologize first.

options.text: Red is also nice.
options.feedback: Do not argue with the customer's choice. He wanted blue.

step2.text: Check my order? It is clear! I wanted blue!

options.text: You are right, sir. I see here that you ordered a blue shirt. It was our error in packing. I apologize for the inconvenience.
Maybe you ordered red.
options.feedback: Do not blame the customer if you see the error. Admit it.

options.text: Calm down.
options.feedback: Telling an angry customer to calm down usually makes them angrier. Apologize instead.

step3.text: Well, I need the blue shirt for a wedding tomorrow! Do you have it?

options.text: Yes, we have the blue shirt in stock. I will get it for you right now. And because of our mistake, I will give you a 10% discount on your next purchase.
I think so.
options.feedback: Be sure and act quickly to solve the problem.

options.text: Wait here.
options.feedback: Explain what you are going to do before leaving him.

step4.text: Okay, that is better. But be more careful next time.

options.text: Here is the blue shirt, sir. Please check it to be sure. Again, I am sorry for the mix-up.
Here.
options.feedback: Be polite and apologize again as you hand him the shirt.

options.text: It happens.
options.feedback: Show you care about quality and customer satisfaction.

step5.text: Yes, this is the right one. Thank you.

options.text: Thank you for your patience, sir. Have a wonderful time at the wedding. Goodbye.
Bye.
options.feedback: End on a positive note.

options.text: Next time order earlier.
options.feedback: Do not lecture the customer. Just say thank you.

scenarios.title: Asking for Clarification in a Meeting
scenarios.description: You are in a meeting at work. Your boss is explaining a new project, but he is speaking very fast and using difficult words. You do not understand one part. You want to ask him to explain it again.

start.text: ...and so we will leverage the synergistic capabilities of the new platform to optimize throughput. Any questions?

options.text: Excuse me, sir. I have a question. Could you please explain the part about 'synergistic capabilities' again? I did not quite catch that.
I don't understand.
options.feedback: Be specific about what you didn't understand.

options.text: You speak too fast.
options.feedback: Be polite. Ask for clarification instead of criticizing his speed.

step2.text: Ah, synergistic capabilities. I mean that the new tools will work together to make the work faster. Does that make sense?

options.text: Yes, that is clearer. So, the tools will be connected to improve speed. Is that correct?
Okay.
options.feedback: Check your understanding by rephrasing what he said.

options.text: Maybe.
options.feedback: If you are not sure, ask again.

step3.text: Exactly. They will share data automatically. This will save us about two hours per day.

options.text: That sounds great. Thank you for clarifying. I understand now.
Two hours?
options.feedback: Show you understand the benefit and thank him.

options.text: I see.
options.feedback: Confirm you understand and thank him.

scenarios.title: Saying Goodbye to a Friend Leaving for Another City
scenarios.description: Your friend is moving to another city for a new job. You are at the bus station to say goodbye.

start.text: Well, the bus is here. I guess this is it.

options.text: I am going to miss you so much! I am sad you are leaving, but I am happy for your new job.
Don't go.
options.feedback: Be supportive of his new opportunity.

options.text: Bye.
options.feedback: Show more emotion. He is a friend.

step2.text: I will miss you too. It is a big change for me.

options.text: You will do great. Remember to call me when you arrive and settle in. We must stay in touch.
Yes.
options.feedback: Encourage him and ask him to keep in touch.

options.text: Don't forget me.
options.feedback: Ask him to call you when he arrives.

step3.text: I promise I will call. And you must come to visit me during the holidays.

options.text: I definitely will! Take care of yourself and have a safe journey. Goodbye, my friend!
Okay.
options.feedback: Promise to visit and wish him a safe journey.

options.text: Good luck.
options.feedback: Say a warm goodbye.
